831	    // MARK: - Drawing
832	
833	    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
834	        DS.canvasVoid.setFill()
835	        bounds.fill()
836	        guard canvasFrame.width > 2 else { return }
837	        // A hairline so a black canvas on a dark void still has an edge.
838	        DS.border.setStroke()
839	        let border = NSBezierPath(rect: canvasFrame.insetBy(dx: -0.5, dy: -0.5))
840	        border.lineWidth = 1
841	        border.stroke()
842	    }
843	
844	    /// The overlay's whole drawing pass. Called by `CanvasOverlayView.draw`,
845	    /// which owns nothing but the event forwarding.
846	    func drawOverlay(in dirtyRect: CGRect) {
847	        guard canvasFrame.width > 2, canvasScale > 0 else { return }
848	        if cropMode, let box = primaryBox { drawCropGhost(box) }
849	        for box in boxes where selection.contains(box.id) {
850	            strokeBox(box, emphasised: box.id == primaryBox?.id)
851	        }
852	        drawObscureRegions()
853	        subjects?.draw(on: self)
854	        if let box = primaryBox, !box.locked, editingClip == nil {
855	            if cropMode {
856	                drawHandles(
857	                    CanvasHandle.allCases.map { box.cropHandlePoint($0) }, fill: DS.snapGuide)
858	            } else {
859	                drawRotationGrip(box)
860	                drawHandles(CanvasHandle.allCases.map { box.handlePoint($0) }, fill: .white)
861	                drawEndpoints(box)
862	            }
863	        }
864	        drawSnapGuides()
865	    }
866	
867	    private func strokeBox(_ box: CanvasLayerBox, emphasised: Bool) {
868	        let path = polygon(box.corners)
869	        // A dark backing stroke first: the coral outline has to survive both a
870	        // white frame and a black one.
871	        NSColor.black.withAlphaComponent(0.4).setStroke()
872	        path.lineWidth = emphasised ? 3 : 2
873	        path.stroke()
874	        DS.playhead.setStroke()
875	        path.lineWidth = emphasised ? 1.5 : 1
876	        path.stroke()
877	    }
878	
879	    /// Crop mode's ghost: everything the crop is removing, dimmed to 30 % of
880	    /// the frame's own contrast. The overlay cannot re-render the source
881	    /// pixels — the player shows the CROPPED composite — so the ghost is the
882	    /// region, drawn as a scrim inside the uncropped rectangle.
883	    private func drawCropGhost(_ box: CanvasLayerBox) {
884	        let outer = polygon(box.corners(of: box.uncroppedRect))
885	        let inner = polygon(box.corners)
886	        let ghost = NSBezierPath()
887	        ghost.append(outer)
888	        ghost.append(inner)
889	        ghost.windingRule = .evenOdd
890	        NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.3).setFill()
891	        ghost.fill()
892	        outer.lineWidth = 1
893	        let dash: [CGFloat] = [4, 3]
894	        outer.setLineDash(dash, count: dash.count, phase: 0)
895	        DS.snapGuide.withAlphaComponent(0.9).setStroke()
896	        outer.stroke()
897	    }
898	
899	    func drawHandles(_ points: [CGPoint], fill: NSColor) {
900	        let side = Self.handleSize
901	        for point in points {
902	            let centre = canvasToView(point)
903	            let rect = CGRect(
904	                x: centre.x - side / 2, y: centre.y - side / 2, width: side, height: side)
905	            let path = NSBezierPath(rect: rect)
906	            fill.setFill()
907	            path.fill()
908	            NSColor.black.withAlphaComponent(0.7).setStroke()
909	            path.lineWidth = 1
910	            path.stroke()
911	        }
912	    }
913	
914	    private func drawRotationGrip(_ box: CanvasLayerBox) {
915	        let offset = canvasDistance(Self.rotationOffset)
916	        let top = canvasToView(box.handlePoint(.top))
917	        let grip = canvasToView(box.rotationHandlePoint(offset: offset))
918	        let stalk = NSBezierPath()
919	        stalk.move(to: top)
920	        stalk.line(to: grip)
921	        stalk.lineWidth = 1
922	        DS.playhead.setStroke()
923	        stalk.stroke()
924	        let radius = Self.handleSize / 2 + 1
925	        let circle = NSBezierPath(
926	            ovalIn: CGRect(
927	                x: grip.x - radius, y: grip.y - radius, width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2))
928	        NSColor.white.setFill()
929	        circle.fill()
930	        DS.playhead.setStroke()
931	        circle.lineWidth = 1.5
932	        circle.stroke()
933	    }
934	
935	    /// Line and arrow shapes get endpoint handles instead of a meaningful box
936	    /// (spec §4.2) — round, so they never read as scale handles.
937	    private func drawEndpoints(_ box: CanvasLayerBox) {
938	        for endpoint in [CanvasEndpoint.from, .to] {
939	            guard let at = box.endpointPoint(endpoint) else { continue }
940	            let centre = canvasToView(at)
941	            let radius = Self.handleSize / 2 + 1
942	            let circle = NSBezierPath(
943	                ovalIn: CGRect(
944	                    x: centre.x - radius, y: centre.y - radius,
945	                    width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2))
946	            DS.marquee.setFill()
947	            circle.fill()
948	            NSColor.white.setStroke()
949	            circle.lineWidth = 1
950	            circle.stroke()
951	        }
952	    }
953	
954	    /// The guides for whichever axes are currently snapped, drawn across the
955	    /// whole canvas so the alignment they claim is visible.
956	    private func drawSnapGuides() {
957	        guard let session = moving, session.guideX != nil || session.guideY != nil else { return }
958	        DS.snapGuide.setStroke()
959	        let canvas = snapshot.canvas
960	        if let x = session.guideX {
961	            let top = canvasToView(CGPoint(x: x, y: 0))
962	            let bottom = canvasToView(CGPoint(x: x, y: CGFloat(canvas.height)))
963	            strokeGuide(from: top, to: bottom)
964	        }
965	        if let y = session.guideY {
966	            let left = canvasToView(CGPoint(x: 0, y: y))
967	            let right = canvasToView(CGPoint(x: CGFloat(canvas.width), y: y))
968	            strokeGuide(from: left, to: right)
969	        }
970	    }
971	
972	    private func strokeGuide(from: CGPoint, to: CGPoint) {
973	        let path = NSBezierPath()
974	        path.move(to: from)
975	        path.line(to: to)
976	        path.lineWidth = 1
977	        path.stroke()
978	    }
979	
980	    func polygon(_ points: [CGPoint]) -> NSBezierPath {
981	        let path = NSBezierPath()
982	        guard let first = points.first else { return path }
983	        path.move(to: canvasToView(first))
984	        for point in points.dropFirst() { path.line(to: canvasToView(point)) }
985	        path.close()
986	        return path
987	    }
988	}

1	import AppKit

3	/// The preview canvas's geometry and its gesture sessions (spec §4.2).
4	///
5	/// Everything here works in CANVAS space — pixels, origin at the canvas's
6	/// top-left, **y growing downward** — which is the space `canvasRect(of:in:
7	/// sourceSize:video:)` and `canvasAnchor(of:in:video:)` in
8	/// `ProjectSnapshot.swift` speak, and the space the frame recipe describes.
9	/// `PreviewCanvasView` owns the one conversion to and from view points
10	/// (`canvasToView` / `viewToCanvas`, mapped through `AVPlayerLayer.videoRect`
11	/// so handles and pixels cannot drift); nothing in this file knows about
12	/// points, zoom or panning.
13	///
14	/// **The pitfall this file exists to avoid:** placement is *not*
15	/// re-derivable. Cropping removes edges in place and rotation happens about
16	/// the *uncropped* centre, so every rectangle comes from `canvasRect` and
17	/// every rotation from `canvasAnchor` — never from a hand-rolled transform.
18	
19	// MARK: - Rotation
20	
21	/// Rotates `vector` by `degrees`. Canvas y grows downward, so a positive
22	/// angle reads CLOCKWISE on screen — the same sense the canvas's hit boxes
23	/// (`CanvasLayerBox`) un-rotate by, which is what keeps overlay hit-testing
24	/// and the compositor's picture the same answer.
25	func canvasRotate(_ vector: CGVector, degrees: Double) -> CGVector {
26	    guard degrees != 0 else { return vector }
27	    let radians = degrees * .pi / 180
28	    let c = cos(radians)
29	    let s = sin(radians)
30	    return CGVector(dx: vector.dx * c - vector.dy * s, dy: vector.dx * s + vector.dy * c)
31	}
32	
33	/// The inverse of `canvasRotate` — a canvas point taken back into the
34	/// layer's own axis-aligned space.
35	func canvasUnrotate(_ vector: CGVector, degrees: Double) -> CGVector {
36	    canvasRotate(vector, degrees: -degrees)
37	}

41	/// One of the eight scale handles of a selection box, named for where it
42	/// sits in the layer's OWN (un-rotated) canvas rect. The canvas is y-down,
43	/// so "top" is the smaller y — exactly what it looks like on screen.
44	enum CanvasHandle: CaseIterable {
45	    case topLeft
46	    case top
47	    case topRight
48	    case right
49	    case bottomRight
50	    case bottom
51	    case bottomLeft
52	    case left
53	
54	    /// Position in the unit square measured from the rect's centre: -1, 0 or
55	    /// +1 on each axis.
56	    var unit: CGPoint {
57	        switch self {
58	        case .topLeft: return CGPoint(x: -1, y: -1)
59	        case .top: return CGPoint(x: 0, y: -1)
60	        case .topRight: return CGPoint(x: 1, y: -1)
61	        case .right: return CGPoint(x: 1, y: 0)
62	        case .bottomRight: return CGPoint(x: 1, y: 1)
63	        case .bottom: return CGPoint(x: 0, y: 1)
64	        case .bottomLeft: return CGPoint(x: -1, y: 1)
65	        case .left: return CGPoint(x: -1, y: 0)
66	        }
67	    }
68	
69	    /// The handle across the box — the point a plain (no-⌥) scale drag pins.
70	    var opposite: CanvasHandle {
71	        switch self {
72	        case .topLeft: return .bottomRight
73	        case .top: return .bottom
74	        case .topRight: return .bottomLeft
75	        case .right: return .left
76	        case .bottomRight: return .topLeft
77	        case .bottom: return .top
78	        case .bottomLeft: return .topRight
79	        case .left: return .right
80	        }
81	    }
82	
83	    /// Corners drive both axes; edge midpoints drive one.
84	    var isCorner: Bool { unit.x != 0 && unit.y != 0 }
85	    var drivesX: Bool { unit.x != 0 }
86	    var drivesY: Bool { unit.y != 0 }
87	
88	    /// Where the handle sits on `rect`, in the rect's own (un-rotated) space.
89	    func point(in rect: CGRect) -> CGPoint {
90	        CGPoint(
91	            x: rect.midX + unit.x * rect.width / 2,
92	            y: rect.midY + unit.y * rect.height / 2)
93	    }
94	
95	    /// AppKit has no diagonal resize cursor in its public API, so corners get
96	    /// the crosshair rather than a cursor that lies about the axis.
97	    var cursor: NSCursor {
98	        if isCorner { return .crosshair }
99	        return drivesX ? .resizeLeftRight : .resizeUpDown
100	    }
101	}

107	    case to

124	// MARK: - A layer's box on the canvas
125	
126	/// One frame-recipe layer paired with the clip it came from and the source
127	/// size the platform measured for it — everything the overlay needs to draw
128	/// a box, hit-test it, or snap to it.
129	///
130	/// The recipe carries EVALUATED properties (actions already applied, §5.4),
131	/// which is what must be drawn; the ops a gesture emits are written against
132	/// the target's props instead (`CanvasEditTarget`: the base, or the selected
133	/// action's end state), never the playhead's interpolated value.
134	struct CanvasLayerBox {
135	    let clip: ClipSnapshot
136	    let canvas: CanvasSnapshot
137	    /// The layer's evaluated video properties (`RecipeLayer.videoProps`).
138	    let video: VideoProps
139	    /// Uncropped source size: media pixels, the shape box, or the measured
140	    /// text layout box (`LayerRenderers.measuredSize(for:)`).
141	    let sourceSize: CGSize
142	    /// A locked track is drawn but never hit (spec §4.2).
143	    let locked: Bool
144	
145	    var id: UInt32 { clip.id }
146	    var rotation: Double { video.rotation }
147	
148	    /// The rotation centre — the centre of the UNCROPPED rectangle. Cropping
149	    /// never moves it, which is exactly why it is its own function.
150	    var anchor: CGPoint { canvasAnchor(of: clip, in: canvas, video: video) }
151	
152	    /// The cropped rectangle, un-rotated: what the compositor draws pixels
153	    /// into, and what the eight handles hang off.
154	    var rect: CGRect {
155	        canvasRect(of: clip, in: canvas, sourceSize: sourceSize, video: video)
156	    }
157	
158	    /// The same rectangle with the crop taken out — the crop-mode ghost, and
159	    /// the box a shape's unit-space endpoints are measured in.
160	    var uncroppedRect: CGRect {
161	        canvasRect(of: clip, in: canvas, sourceSize: sourceSize, video: video.uncropped)
162	    }
163	
164	    /// A point in the layer's axis-aligned space, taken into canvas space.
165	    func rotated(_ point: CGPoint) -> CGPoint {
166	        let a = anchor
167	        let v = canvasRotate(
168	            CGVector(dx: point.x - a.x, dy: point.y - a.y), degrees: rotation)
169	        return CGPoint(x: a.x + v.dx, y: a.y + v.dy)
170	    }
171	
172	    /// A canvas point taken back into the layer's axis-aligned space, where
173	    /// `rect` and the crop insets live.
174	    func unrotated(_ point: CGPoint) -> CGPoint {
175	        let a = anchor
176	        let v = canvasUnrotate(
177	            CGVector(dx: point.x - a.x, dy: point.y - a.y), degrees: rotation)
178	        return CGPoint(x: a.x + v.dx, y: a.y + v.dy)
179	    }
180	
181	    /// Hit test in canvas space, rotation included.
182	    func contains(_ point: CGPoint) -> Bool { rect.contains(unrotated(point)) }
183	
184	    /// The cropped rectangle's four corners in canvas space, TL TR BR BL.
185	    var corners: [CGPoint] { corners(of: rect) }
186	
187	    func corners(of box: CGRect) -> [CGPoint] {
188	        [
189	            rotated(CGPoint(x: box.minX, y: box.minY)),
190	            rotated(CGPoint(x: box.maxX, y: box.minY)),
191	            rotated(CGPoint(x: box.maxX, y: box.maxY)),
192	            rotated(CGPoint(x: box.minX, y: box.maxY)),
193	        ]
194	    }
195	
196	    /// The axis-aligned bounds of the ROTATED box — what snapping and the
197	    /// visible-extent tests use, so a turned clip still offers sane edges.
198	    var bounds: CGRect {
199	        let points = corners
200	        guard let first = points.first else { return rect }
201	        var minX = first.x, maxX = first.x, minY = first.y, maxY = first.y
202	        for point in points.dropFirst() {
203	            minX = min(minX, point.x)
204	            maxX = max(maxX, point.x)
205	            minY = min(minY, point.y)
206	            maxY = max(maxY, point.y)
207	        }
208	        return CGRect(x: minX, y: minY, width: maxX - minX, height: maxY - minY)
209	    }
210	
211	    func handlePoint(_ handle: CanvasHandle) -> CGPoint { rotated(handle.point(in: rect)) }
212	
213	    func cropHandlePoint(_ handle: CanvasHandle) -> CGPoint { handlePoint(handle) }
214	
215	    /// The rotation grip, `offset` canvas pixels beyond the top edge along
216	    /// the box's own "up".
217	    func rotationHandlePoint(offset: CGFloat) -> CGPoint {
218	        let up = canvasRotate(CGVector(dx: 0, dy: -1), degrees: rotation)
219	        let top = handlePoint(.top)
220	        return CGPoint(x: top.x + up.dx * offset, y: top.y + up.dy * offset)
221	    }
222	
223	    /// A line/arrow endpoint in canvas space. Endpoints are UNIT coordinates
224	    /// in the uncropped box (`ShapeProps.from` / `.to`).
225	    func endpointPoint(_ endpoint: CanvasEndpoint) -> CGPoint? {
226	        guard let shape = clip.shape, shape.kind.isLinear else { return nil }
227	        let unit = endpoint == .from ? shape.fromPoint : shape.toPoint
228	        let box = uncroppedRect
229	        return rotated(
230	            CGPoint(x: box.minX + unit.x * box.width, y: box.minY + unit.y * box.height))
231	    }
232	
233	    /// The inverse: a canvas point as unit coordinates in the uncropped box,
234	    /// clamped to it.
235	    func endpointUnit(_ point: CGPoint) -> CGPoint {
236	        let box = uncroppedRect
237	        guard box.width > 0, box.height > 0 else { return .zero }
238	        let local = unrotated(point)
239	        return CGPoint(
240	            x: min(max((local.x - box.minX) / box.width, 0), 1),
241	            y: min(max((local.y - box.minY) / box.height, 0), 1))
242	    }

244	    // MARK: The region frame
245	
246	    /// A canvas point as SOURCE pixels measured from the centre of the
247	    /// layer's CROPPED rect — the frame `video.spotlight`, `video.obscure`
248	    /// and `add_zoom_action`'s region all speak (`model_regions.rs`'s
249	    /// `Spotlight`, and `Compositor.metal`'s
250	    /// `centre = cropped * 0.5 + float2(spotX, spotY)`). Spec §5.3 calls it Q.
251	    ///
252	    /// **It reads the EVALUATED props, and that is the opposite of every
253	    /// gesture session in this file.** Move, Scale, Rotate and Crop all
254	    /// capture the target's props at mouse-down (`CanvasEditTarget.start`),
255	    /// because the op merges into them and a clip inside an action must not
256	    /// be baked to its animated value. A region is measured the other way round: the
257	    /// user drags over what is ON SCREEN, and a source-pixel answer is
258	    /// transform-invariant only if the un-transform matches the transform
259	    /// that drew it. `video` here IS the recipe's evaluated state, so a clip
260	    /// already inside an action scaling it 2× yields the region the user
261	    /// drew rather than half of it — and it agrees by construction with
262	    /// `edit_zoom.rs`, which reads the clip evaluated at the action's start.
263	    /// The two readings differ only once a clip has actions, which is
264	    /// exactly when a zoom action is being added to it.
265	    func sourcePoint(_ point: CGPoint) -> CGPoint {
266	        let local = unrotated(point)
267	        let box = rect
268	        let s = video.scale > 0 ? video.scale : 1
269	        return CGPoint(x: (local.x - box.midX) / s, y: (local.y - box.midY) / s)
270	    }
271	
272	    /// The inverse of `sourcePoint`: a point in the layer's own source-pixel
273	    /// frame, back on the canvas — what draws a stored region where its
274	    /// pixels are.
275	    func canvasPoint(source point: CGPoint) -> CGPoint {
276	        let box = rect
277	        let s = video.scale > 0 ? video.scale : 1
278	        return rotated(CGPoint(x: box.midX + point.x * s, y: box.midY + point.y * s))
279	    }
280	
281	    /// A rectangle in the source-pixel frame as its four canvas-space
282	    /// corners, TL TR BR BL — `corners(of:)`'s twin, for the one shape that
283	    /// is axis-aligned in the LAYER's axes rather than in the canvas's.
284	    func canvasQuad(ofSource box: CGRect) -> [CGPoint] {
285	        [
286	            canvasPoint(source: CGPoint(x: box.minX, y: box.minY)),
287	            canvasPoint(source: CGPoint(x: box.maxX, y: box.minY)),
288	            canvasPoint(source: CGPoint(x: box.maxX, y: box.maxY)),
289	            canvasPoint(source: CGPoint(x: box.minX, y: box.maxY)),
290	        ]
291	    }

293	    // MARK: Building
294	
295	    /// The boxes of one composed frame, back to front — the recipe's own
296	    /// order, which is the order the compositor draws in and the reverse of
297	    /// the order the canvas hit-tests in.
298	    static func boxes(recipe: FrameRecipe, snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> [CanvasLayerBox] {
299	        recipe.layers.compactMap { layer in
300	            guard let clip = snapshot.clip(layer.clip) else { return nil }
301	            guard let size = LayerRenderers.measuredSize(for: layer)
302	                ?? snapshot.sourceSize(of: clip), size.width > 0, size.height > 0
303	            else { return nil }
304	            return CanvasLayerBox(
305	                clip: clip, canvas: snapshot.canvas, video: layer.videoProps, sourceSize: size,
306	                locked: snapshot.track(clip.track)?.locked ?? false)
307	        }
308	    }
309	
310	    /// The degraded path, used only when the core cannot answer with a
311	    /// recipe: the same list from the snapshot alone, with base props and no
312	    /// action evaluation. Text is measured the same way, so a text clip still
313	    /// gets a box.
314	    static func boxes(snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, at time: Ticks) -> [CanvasLayerBox] {
315	        snapshot.layers(at: time).compactMap { clip in
316	            var size = snapshot.sourceSize(of: clip)
317	            if size == nil, let text = clip.text {
318	                size = LayerRenderers.measuredSize(for: text)
319	            }
320	            guard let resolved = size, resolved.width > 0, resolved.height > 0 else { return nil }
321	            return CanvasLayerBox(
322	                clip: clip, canvas: snapshot.canvas, video: clip.videoProps, sourceSize: resolved,
323	                locked: snapshot.track(clip.track)?.locked ?? false)
324	        }
325	    }

328	// MARK: - Snapping
329	
330	/// Spec §4.2's canvas snapping: the canvas centre lines, its edges, its
331	/// thirds, and every other visible layer's edges and centres.
332	///
333	/// The candidates are computed here in Swift from the layer rects — the core
334	/// has no idea where anything sits on screen — but the nearest-within-
335	/// threshold *pick* is `ReelSnap.resolve` (i.e. `rc_snap_resolve`), so the
336	/// canvas and the timeline snap by the same rule. That function speaks in
337	/// `Ticks`, so canvas coordinates are rounded to whole pixels on the way in;
338	/// a snap is always to a pixel, which is what the guides promise anyway.
339	struct CanvasSnapper {
340	    /// Grab radius in VIEW points, converted to canvas pixels per zoom.
341	    static let threshold: CGFloat = 8
342	
343	    let xs: [Ticks]
344	    let ys: [Ticks]
345	    /// The radius in canvas pixels at the current zoom.
346	    let threshold: Ticks
347	    /// Folds together the N toggle and the ⌘ suppression, so no session ever
348	    /// looks at modifier flags itself.
349	    let enabled: Bool
350	
351	    /// What a proposed rectangle has to move by to sit on a candidate, plus
352	    /// the guide lines to draw (canvas coordinates, nil when nothing snapped).
353	    struct Result {
354	        var offset = CGVector.zero
355	        var guideX: CGFloat?
356	        var guideY: CGFloat?
357	    }
358	
359	    /// Tries the rectangle's leading edge, centre and trailing edge on each
360	    /// axis and takes the smallest correction of the three.
361	    func resolve(rect: CGRect) -> Result {
362	        var result = Result()
363	        guard enabled else { return result }
364	        if let hit = best(of: [rect.minX, rect.midX, rect.maxX], in: xs) {
365	            result.offset.dx = hit.delta
366	            result.guideX = hit.guide
367	        }
368	        if let hit = best(of: [rect.minY, rect.midY, rect.maxY], in: ys) {
369	            result.offset.dy = hit.delta
370	            result.guideY = hit.guide
371	        }
372	        return result
373	    }
374	
375	    private func best(
376	        of anchors: [CGFloat], in candidates: [Ticks]
377	    ) -> (delta: CGFloat, guide: CGFloat)? {
378	        var winner: (delta: CGFloat, guide: CGFloat)?
379	        for anchor in anchors {
380	            let (resolved, snapped) = ReelSnap.resolve(
381	                candidates, CanvasSnapper.tick(anchor), threshold: threshold)
382	            guard snapped else { continue }
383	            let delta = CGFloat(resolved) - anchor
384	            if let current = winner, abs(current.delta) <= abs(delta) { continue }
385	            winner = (delta, CGFloat(resolved))
386	        }
387	        return winner
388	    }
389	
390	    /// A canvas coordinate as a whole pixel, clamped well inside `Int64` so a
391	    /// runaway drag cannot trap the conversion.
392	    static func tick(_ value: CGFloat) -> Ticks {
393	        guard value.isFinite else { return 0 }
394	        return Ticks(min(max(value.rounded(), -1e9), 1e9))
395	    }
396	
397	    /// Canvas landmarks plus the other layers'. `excluding` is the clips the
398	    /// gesture is moving — a drag must not snap to itself.
399	    static func candidates(
400	        boxes: [CanvasLayerBox], excluding: Set<UInt32>, canvas: CanvasSnapshot
401	    ) -> (xs: [Ticks], ys: [Ticks]) {
402	        let width = CGFloat(canvas.width)
403	        let height = CGFloat(canvas.height)
404	        var xs: Set<Ticks> = [
405	            tick(0), tick(width / 3), tick(width / 2), tick(width * 2 / 3), tick(width),
406	        ]
407	        var ys: Set<Ticks> = [
408	            tick(0), tick(height / 3), tick(height / 2), tick(height * 2 / 3), tick(height),
409	        ]
410	        for box in boxes where !excluding.contains(box.id) {
411	            let bounds = box.bounds
412	            xs.formUnion([tick(bounds.minX), tick(bounds.midX), tick(bounds.maxX)])
413	            ys.formUnion([tick(bounds.minY), tick(bounds.midY), tick(bounds.maxY)])
414	        }
415	        return (xs.sorted(), ys.sorted())
416	    }
417	}

419	/// Trims a canvas coordinate to three decimals before it goes into an op.
420	/// Snapping produces whole or half pixels; this only keeps float noise out of
421	/// the project JSON, where it would make two identical edits compare unequal.
422	func canvasRound(_ value: Double) -> Double {
423	    guard value.isFinite else { return 0 }
424	    return (value * 1000).rounded() / 1000
425	}
426	
427	/// A colour as `video.chroma.key`: exactly three components, clamped to 0…1.
428	///
429	/// That key is the ONE colour in the schema the model spells without an alpha
430	/// (`[f64; 3]` in `model.rs`, and `props_check.rs` bounds each channel), so a
431	/// four-component `RGBA` — which is what a colour well hands back, and what
432	/// the comparison in `changedRGBA` needs — has to be cut back to three before
433	/// it can reach `set_video`. A longer array is not a warning there: serde
434	/// answers `invalid length 4, expected an array of length 3` and the whole
435	/// edit fails.
436	func chromaKeyComponents(_ color: RGBA) -> [Double] {
437	    (0..<3).map { index in
438	        let value = index < color.count ? color[index] : 0
439	        return canvasRound(min(max(value, 0), 1))
440	    }
441	}

443	// MARK: - Move
444	
445	/// Dragging inside the box to move the selection (spec §4.2). Every selected
446	/// clip moves by the same canvas-space delta; the anchor clip's rectangle is
447	/// what snapping tests, so the whole selection clicks into place together.
448	///
449	/// The op writes the target's props plus the delta (the base, or the selected
450	/// action's end state — CI-13), never the evaluated position at the playhead.
451	struct CanvasMoveSession {
452	    /// The target's `(x, y)` per clip, captured at mouse-down.
453	    let bases: [UInt32: CGPoint]
454	    let anchor: UInt32
455	    /// The anchor's rotated bounds at mouse-down.
456	    let anchorBounds: CGRect
457	    /// Pointer position at mouse-down, canvas space.
458	    let grab: CGPoint
459	
460	    var delta = CGVector.zero
461	    var guideX: CGFloat?
462	    var guideY: CGFloat?
463	    /// False until the pointer actually leaves the press point — a click that
464	    /// only selects must not register an undo step.
465	    var didMove = false
466	
467	    /// One op per clip, routed by `target`: each keeps its own position, so
468	    /// a multi-clip move cannot collapse the selection onto one point.
469	    func ops(to target: CanvasEditTarget) -> [ReelOp] {
470	        bases.keys.sorted().compactMap { id in
471	            guard let base = bases[id] else { return nil }
472	            return target.op(
473	                video: VideoPatch(
474	                    x: canvasRound(base.x + delta.dx), y: canvasRound(base.y + delta.dy)),
475	                clip: id)
476	        }
477	    }
478	
479	    mutating func update(point: CGPoint, snapper: CanvasSnapper) {
480	        var raw = CGVector(dx: point.x - grab.x, dy: point.y - grab.y)
481	        let proposed = anchorBounds.offsetBy(dx: raw.dx, dy: raw.dy)
482	        let result = snapper.resolve(rect: proposed)
483	        raw.dx += result.offset.dx
484	        raw.dy += result.offset.dy
485	        delta = raw
486	        guideX = result.guideX
487	        guideY = result.guideY
488	        didMove = true
489	    }
490	}

492	// MARK: - Scale
493	
494	/// What a scale drag is allowed to change, which depends on what the model
495	/// stores for that clip (§5.2).
496	///
497	/// **The pitfall:** a clip has ONE uniform `scale` — there is no per-axis
498	/// scale for pixels. So "edges scale one axis" and "⇧ frees the aspect" can
499	/// only be honoured where the model owns a second number: a shape's
500	/// `width`/`height`, or a text clip's wrap `width`. Everywhere else a drag
501	/// stays uniform rather than pretending otherwise.
502	enum CanvasScaleTarget: Equatable {
503	    /// Media, stills, images, nests — `video.scale` only.
504	    case uniform
505	    /// A shape's box, in model units.
506	    case box(CGSize)
507	    /// A text clip's wrap width (nil = auto-sized); the measured width at
508	    /// mouse-down stands in for it.
509	    case textWidth(Double)
510	}
511	
512	/// One clip resized by one of the eight handles (spec §4.2). ⌥ scales about
513	/// the centre; without it the opposite handle is pinned, which means the
514	/// clip's position moves too — hence the `x`/`y` in the patch.
515	struct CanvasScaleSession {
516	    let clip: UInt32
517	    let handle: CanvasHandle
518	    let target: CanvasScaleTarget
519	    /// The target's video props at mouse-down (`CanvasEditTarget.start`).
520	    let base: VideoProps
521	    /// The uncropped rectangle at mouse-down, un-rotated, canvas space. Its
522	    /// centre IS the rotation anchor, which is what makes the position
523	    /// correction below a plain rotation of the centre's displacement.
524	    let startRect: CGRect
525	    let rotation: Double
526	
527	    var scale: Double
528	    var boxSize: CGSize
529	    var textWidth: Double
530	    /// True once a `.textWidth` drag has actually taken the width path. The
531	    /// other six handles of a text clip fall back to a uniform scale, and
532	    /// `ops` must then emit `set_video` rather than `set_text`.
533	    var widthOnly = false
534	    /// Change in the clip's `(x, y)`, canvas space.
535	    var offset = CGVector.zero
536	    var didMove = false
537	
538	    static let minScale = 0.01
539	    static let maxScale = 10.0
540	    static let minBox = 4.0
541	    static let maxBox = 20000.0
542	
543	    func ops(to edit: CanvasEditTarget) -> [ReelOp] {
544	        let placement = VideoPatch(
545	            x: canvasRound(base.x + offset.dx), y: canvasRound(base.y + offset.dy))
546	        var uniform = placement
547	        uniform.scale = canvasRound(scale)
548	        switch target {
549	        case .uniform:
550	            return [edit.op(video: uniform, clip: clip)]
551	        case .box:
552	            // Base whatever `edit` says (CI-13): `set_shape` has no action
553	            // form, and the placement that pins the pivot travels with it.
554	            return [
555	                .setShape(
556	                    clips: [clip],
557	                    patch: ShapePatch(
558	                        width: canvasRound(boxSize.width), height: canvasRound(boxSize.height))),
559	                .setVideo(clips: [clip], patch: placement),
560	            ]
561	        case .textWidth:
562	            guard widthOnly else { return [edit.op(video: uniform, clip: clip)] }
563	            return [edit.op(text: TextPatch(width: .some(canvasRound(textWidth))), clip: clip)]
564	        }
565	    }
566	
567	    /// `point` is the pointer in canvas space; `aspectFree` is ⇧ and
568	    /// `aboutCentre` is ⌥.
569	    mutating func update(point: CGPoint, aspectFree: Bool, aboutCentre: Bool) {
570	        let centre = CGPoint(x: startRect.midX, y: startRect.midY)
571	        let grip = handle.point(in: startRect)
572	        let pivot = aboutCentre ? centre : handle.opposite.point(in: startRect)
573	        // The pointer, taken back into the layer's own axis-aligned space —
574	        // the space `startRect` and the handles live in.
575	        let local = unrotatedPoint(point, about: centre)
576	
577	        let dx0 = grip.x - pivot.x
578	        let dy0 = grip.y - pivot.y
579	        let dx = local.x - pivot.x
580	        let dy = local.y - pivot.y
581	        let axisX = abs(dx0) > 0.001 ? dx / dx0 : 1
582	        let axisY = abs(dy0) > 0.001 ? dy / dy0 : 1
583	        let square = dx0 * dx0 + dy0 * dy0
584	        let diagonal = square > 0.001 ? (dx * dx0 + dy * dy0) / square : 1
585	
586	        var fx: CGFloat = 1
587	        var fy: CGFloat = 1
588	        switch target {
589	        case .uniform:
590	            let f = handle.isCorner ? diagonal : (handle.drivesX ? axisX : axisY)
591	            let clamped = min(
592	                max(base.scale * Double(f), CanvasScaleSession.minScale),
593	                CanvasScaleSession.maxScale)
594	            scale = clamped
595	            let applied = base.scale > 0 ? clamped / base.scale : 1
596	            fx = CGFloat(applied)
597	            fy = fx
598	
599	        case .box(let start):
600	            var wide = start.width
601	            var high = start.height
602	            if handle.isCorner {
603	                wide = start.width * Double(aspectFree ? axisX : diagonal)
604	                high = start.height * Double(aspectFree ? axisY : diagonal)
605	            } else if handle.drivesX {
606	                wide = start.width * Double(axisX)
607	            } else {
608	                high = start.height * Double(axisY)
609	            }
610	            boxSize = CGSize(
611	                width: min(max(wide, CanvasScaleSession.minBox), CanvasScaleSession.maxBox),
612	                height: min(max(high, CanvasScaleSession.minBox), CanvasScaleSession.maxBox))
613	            fx = start.width > 0 ? CGFloat(boxSize.width / start.width) : 1
614	            fy = start.height > 0 ? CGFloat(boxSize.height / start.height) : 1
615	
616	        case .textWidth(let start):
617	            guard handle.drivesX, !handle.isCorner else {
618	                // Corners and the top/bottom edges have no second axis to
619	                // give a text clip, so they scale it uniformly instead.
620	                let f = handle.isCorner ? diagonal : axisY
621	                scale = min(
622	                    max(base.scale * Double(f), CanvasScaleSession.minScale),
623	                    CanvasScaleSession.maxScale)
624	                let applied = base.scale > 0 ? scale / base.scale : 1
625	                widthOnly = false
626	                apply(fx: CGFloat(applied), fy: CGFloat(applied), pivot: pivot, centre: centre)
627	                didMove = true
628	                return
629	            }
630	            widthOnly = true
631	            textWidth = min(
632	                max(start * Double(axisX), CanvasScaleSession.minBox),
633	                CanvasScaleSession.maxBox)
634	            // The measured box includes backdrop padding and outline
635	            // overshoot, so the pivot cannot be held exactly; the centre stays
636	            // put and the text grows both ways.
637	            offset = .zero
638	            didMove = true
639	            return
640	        }
641	        apply(fx: fx, fy: fy, pivot: pivot, centre: centre)
642	        didMove = true
643	    }
644	
645	    /// Holds `pivot` still while the box scales by `(fx, fy)`: the centre
646	    /// moves in the layer's own space, and that displacement is rotated back
647	    /// into canvas space to become the clip's new `(x, y)`.
648	    private mutating func apply(fx: CGFloat, fy: CGFloat, pivot: CGPoint, centre: CGPoint) {
649	        let moved = CGPoint(
650	            x: pivot.x + (centre.x - pivot.x) * fx,
651	            y: pivot.y + (centre.y - pivot.y) * fy)
652	        offset = canvasRotate(
653	            CGVector(dx: moved.x - centre.x, dy: moved.y - centre.y), degrees: rotation)
654	    }
655	
656	    private func unrotatedPoint(_ point: CGPoint, about centre: CGPoint) -> CGPoint {
657	        let v = canvasUnrotate(
658	            CGVector(dx: point.x - centre.x, dy: point.y - centre.y), degrees: rotation)
659	        return CGPoint(x: centre.x + v.dx, y: centre.y + v.dy)
660	    }
661	}

663	// MARK: - Rotate
664	
665	/// The grip above the top edge (spec §4.2). ⇧ snaps to 15°.
666	struct CanvasRotateSession {
667	    let clip: UInt32
668	    let base: VideoProps
669	    /// The rotation centre, canvas space — `canvasAnchor`, never the cropped
670	    /// rectangle's middle.
671	    let anchor: CGPoint
672	    /// The pointer's angle at mouse-down, radians.
673	    let grabAngle: Double
674	
675	    var rotation: Double
676	    var didMove = false
677	
678	    static let snapDegrees = 15.0
679	
680	    func op(to target: CanvasEditTarget) -> ReelOp {
681	        target.op(video: VideoPatch(rotation: canvasRound(rotation)), clip: clip)
682	    }
683	
684	    mutating func update(point: CGPoint, snapping: Bool) {
685	        let angle = atan2(Double(point.y - anchor.y), Double(point.x - anchor.x))
686	        var degrees = base.rotation + (angle - grabAngle) * 180 / .pi
687	        if snapping {
688	            degrees = (degrees / CanvasRotateSession.snapDegrees).rounded()
689	                * CanvasRotateSession.snapDegrees
690	        }
691	        // Kept in (-180, 180] so the inspector never shows 4 000°.
692	        degrees = degrees.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 360)
693	        if degrees > 180 { degrees -= 360 }
694	        if degrees <= -180 { degrees += 360 }
695	        rotation = degrees
696	        didMove = true
697	    }
698	
699	    /// The angle a press at `point` makes about `anchor` — what a session is
700	    /// constructed with so the grip does not jump to the pointer.
701	    static func angle(of point: CGPoint, about anchor: CGPoint) -> Double {
702	        atan2(Double(point.y - anchor.y), Double(point.x - anchor.x))
703	    }
704	}

706	// MARK: - Crop
707	
708	/// Crop mode's handles (spec §4.2): the same eight positions, but each one
709	/// drives a crop inset in SOURCE pixels instead of the layer's size.
710	///
711	/// Cropping never shifts content (§5.3), so this session writes `crop` and
712	/// nothing else — no compensating `x`/`y`, ever.
713	struct CanvasCropSession {
714	    let clip: UInt32
715	    let handle: CanvasHandle
716	    let base: VideoProps
717	    let sourceSize: CGSize
718	    /// The uncropped rectangle at mouse-down, un-rotated, canvas space.
719	    let startRect: CGRect
720	    let rotation: Double
721	
722	    var crop: CropInsets
723	    var didMove = false
724	
725	    /// A crop may never close a rectangle completely; one source pixel is the
726	    /// floor, which is also what the core enforces.
727	    static let minRemaining = 1.0
728	
729	    func op(to target: CanvasEditTarget) -> ReelOp {
730	        target.op(video: VideoPatch(crop: crop), clip: clip)
731	    }
732	
733	    mutating func update(point: CGPoint) {
734	        let centre = CGPoint(x: startRect.midX, y: startRect.midY)
735	        let v = canvasUnrotate(
736	            CGVector(dx: point.x - centre.x, dy: point.y - centre.y), degrees: rotation)
737	        let local = CGPoint(x: centre.x + v.dx, y: centre.y + v.dy)
738	        let scale = base.scale > 0 ? base.scale : 1
739	        // Source pixels from the uncropped rectangle's top-left corner.
740	        let sx = Double(local.x - startRect.minX) / scale
741	        let sy = Double(local.y - startRect.minY) / scale
742	
743	        var l = crop.l
744	        var t = crop.t
745	        var r = crop.r
746	        var b = crop.b
747	        let limit = CanvasCropSession.minRemaining
748	        if handle.unit.x < 0 { l = min(max(sx, 0), max(sourceSize.width - r - limit, 0)) }
749	        if handle.unit.x > 0 {
750	            r = min(max(sourceSize.width - sx, 0), max(sourceSize.width - l - limit, 0))
751	        }
752	        if handle.unit.y < 0 { t = min(max(sy, 0), max(sourceSize.height - b - limit, 0)) }
753	        if handle.unit.y > 0 {
754	            b = min(max(sourceSize.height - sy, 0), max(sourceSize.height - t - limit, 0))
755	        }
756	        crop = CropInsets(
757	            l: canvasRound(l), t: canvasRound(t), r: canvasRound(r), b: canvasRound(b))
758	        didMove = true
759	    }
760	}

788	// MARK: - Chroma-key eyedropper
789	
790	/// Picking the chroma key colour off the canvas (spec §4.3's "key color with
791	/// a canvas eyedropper"). One click, not a drag — and a session all the same,
792	/// because the sample cannot be taken while that click is being handled.
793	///
794	/// The preview's pixels belong to the Metal compositor, not to any view, so
795	/// the honest way to read one is to compose the frame again offline
796	/// (`Exporter.renderFrame` — the same `AVComposition` the export writes from,
797	/// so the pixel picked is the pixel the file would hold). That render opens
798	/// asset tracks and decodes, which has to happen off the main thread, and by
799	/// the time it lands the selection may have moved. Everything the click meant
800	/// is therefore captured here first: `EditorViewController+Eyedropper.swift`
801	/// runs it and compares this against the selection before it commits.
802	struct CanvasEyedropperSession {
803	    /// The clips the pick will key — the Video pane's video clips, in the
804	    /// order it offers them.
805	    let clips: [UInt32]
806	    /// The chroma those clips already carry, so a re-pick replaces the colour
807	    /// and keeps the tolerances the user dialled in.
808	    let base: ChromaProps?
809	
810	    /// The op that makes the frame this samples FROM. Applied to a COPY of
811	    /// the project — pure, never published, never on the undo stack, the way
812	    /// `EditorViewController+Inspector`'s probe is (§5.5).
813	    ///
814	    /// It removes the three things standing between the pixel on screen and
815	    /// the number `Compositor.metal` actually compares against the key:
816	    ///
817	    ///  - the clip's own chroma, because a keyed pixel is a HOLE — the most
818	    ///    natural pick of all, "the green I can still see", would otherwise
819	    ///    sample whatever shows through it;
820	    ///  - its colour adjustment, tone, wheels, curves and look (GR-2, GR-11, GR-12, GR-7), as
821	    ///    the shader keys BEFORE them (§7.5's order of operations), so the adjusted pixel
822	    ///    is not the one being compared;
823	    ///  - its opacity, because a faded layer's pixel on screen is already
824	    ///    mixed with whatever lies behind it.
825	    ///
826	    /// What is left is a layer drawn exactly as the key sees it. A layer
827	    /// COVERED by another one is still covered — the pick is what is visible
828	    /// at that point, which is what a user aiming at it means.
829	    var suppression: ReelOp {
830	        .setVideo(clips: clips, patch: VideoPatch(
831	            opacity: 1, color: ColorPatch(.identity), chroma: .some(nil),
832	            look: .some(nil), wheels: .neutral, curves: .reset))
833	    }
834	
835	    /// The sampled colour as the props to write. A first pick keeps
836	    /// `Chroma::default`'s tolerances (0.2 / 0.1 / 0.5, `model.rs`), which is
837	    /// also what the section's on-switch writes.
838	    func chroma(picked color: RGBA) -> ChromaProps {
839	        let previous = base ?? ChromaProps()
840	        return ChromaProps(
841	            key: chromaKeyComponents(color), tolerance: previous.tolerance,
842	            softness: previous.softness, spill: previous.spill)
843	    }
844	
845	    /// The colour of the canvas pixel at `point` in a frame composed from
846	    /// `canvas`, or nil when there is nothing there to pick.
847	    ///
848	    /// **The rendered frame is not the canvas.** Its size is whatever the
849	    /// composition asked for, so a canvas coordinate indexes it as a
850	    /// FRACTION and never as a pixel number; get that wrong and a project
851	    /// whose plan was built for another canvas size picks the wrong colour
852	    /// silently. Its rows do run top-down, which is the same sense canvas
853	    /// space does, so no flip belongs here.
854	    ///
855	    /// The readback is sRGB. The shader compares the values the decoder
856	    /// handed it, so a wide-gamut source can put a pick a per cent or two
857	    /// off the number the key needs — which is what `tolerance` is for, and
858	    /// why the pick sets a colour rather than a threshold.
859	    static func color(at point: CGPoint, in frame: CGImage, canvas: CanvasSnapshot) -> RGBA? {
860	        let size = canvas.size
861	        guard size.width >= 1, size.height >= 1, frame.width >= 1, frame.height >= 1 else {
862	            return nil
863	        }
864	        let column = Int((point.x / size.width * CGFloat(frame.width)).rounded(.down))
865	        let row = Int((point.y / size.height * CGFloat(frame.height)).rounded(.down))
866	        guard column >= 0, row >= 0, column < frame.width, row < frame.height else { return nil }
867	        guard let pixel = frame.cropping(to: CGRect(x: column, y: row, width: 1, height: 1)),
868	              let space = CGColorSpace(name: CGColorSpace.sRGB)
869	        else { return nil }
870	
871	        var bytes = [UInt8](repeating: 0, count: 4)
872	        let drawn = bytes.withUnsafeMutableBytes { raw -> Bool in
873	            guard let base = raw.baseAddress,
874	                  let context = CGContext(
875	                      data: base, width: 1, height: 1, bitsPerComponent: 8, bytesPerRow: 4,
876	                      space: space, bitmapInfo: CGImageAlphaInfo.premultipliedLast.rawValue)
877	            else { return false }
878	            context.draw(pixel, in: CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 1, height: 1))
879	            return true
880	        }
881	        guard drawn else { return nil }
882	        let alpha = Double(bytes[3]) / 255
883	        // Nothing on the canvas there. Refused rather than picked: a
884	        // transparent pixel un-premultiplies to black, and keying black is
885	        // never what a click on empty canvas meant.
886	        guard alpha > 0 else { return nil }
887	        return (0..<3).map { min(Double(bytes[$0]) / 255 / alpha, 1) }
888	    }
889	}

891	// MARK: - Region drags
892	
893	/// What a region dragged on the canvas is FOR (spec §4.2's region mode).
894	///
895	/// One rubber band serves two commits — `add_zoom_action`'s `region` and a
896	/// `video.obscure` entry — because they are the same rectangle in the same
897	/// frame, spec §5.3's Q. A second overlay with a second copy of the maths is
898	/// precisely the drift this file exists to prevent, so the purpose travels
899	/// with the session and `EditorViewController+ZoomRegion.swift` branches on
900	/// it in exactly one place: the commit. The geometry below reads it only to
901	/// say whether the resolved frame is worth drawing.
902	enum CanvasRegionPurpose {
903	    /// `Z`, and the action lane's Zoom to Region button.
904	    case zoom
905	    /// The Obscure section's "Place on Canvas".
906	    case obscure
907	}
908	
909	/// A rectangle dragged over the picture: the region a zoom action lands on,
910	/// or one `video.obscure` entry (spec §4.2, §4.3).
911	///
912	/// Both ends are held in CANVAS pixels — the space this whole file speaks —
913	/// and turned into source pixels only through the layer's box, so a rotated
914	/// or a cropped clip needs no special case here. The band itself drags FREE:
915	/// constraining it to the canvas's aspect would make `fill` unreachable from
916	/// the canvas, since a band that already has the canvas's shape fits and
917	/// fills identically. What keeps that honest is the resolved frame — the
918	/// rectangle that will actually be on screen when the zoom lands — which the
919	/// mode strokes beside the band while the drag is live, the same instinct as
920	/// the crop ghost.
921	struct ZoomRegionSession {
922	    let purpose: CanvasRegionPurpose
923	    /// The clip the region belongs to. The mode is armed for exactly one.
924	    let clip: UInt32
925	    /// Where the press landed, canvas pixels.
926	    let anchor: CGPoint
927	    var current: CGPoint
928	    /// ⇧ held during a ZOOM drag: the region covers the canvas rather than
929	    /// sitting inside it. It means nothing to an obscure region, which is
930	    /// the rectangle it is drawn as.
931	    var fill = false
932	    /// False until the pointer actually leaves the press point — a click
933	    /// that drew no rectangle must commit nothing, the `didMove` flag every
934	    /// session here carries.
935	    var didMove = false
936	
937	    /// The smallest band that counts, in CANVAS pixels. A press with a
938	    /// twitch in it would otherwise ask the core to zoom to a region a
939	    /// fraction of a pixel wide, which is an `Err` naming `region.width`
940	    /// rather than the "nothing happened" it looks like.
941	    static let minBand: CGFloat = 6
942	
943	    /// The dragged rectangle in canvas pixels, however the two corners lie.
944	    var canvasRect: CGRect {
945	        CGRect(
946	            x: min(anchor.x, current.x), y: min(anchor.y, current.y),
947	            width: abs(current.x - anchor.x), height: abs(current.y - anchor.y))
948	    }
949	
950	    /// The flag is raised by MOVEMENT, not by the call: `mouseUp` runs this
951	    /// once more with the release point so the band ends where the pointer
952	    /// did, and a press-and-release that never moved must still read as the
953	    /// click it was.
954	    mutating func update(point: CGPoint, fill: Bool) {
955	        current = point
956	        self.fill = fill
957	        if point != anchor { didMove = true }
958	    }
959	
960	    /// The band as a rectangle in the layer's own source-pixel frame — the
961	    /// min corner and the size, which `region(in:)` turns into the centre
962	    /// and size the op wants. Nil when the drag is too small to mean
963	    /// anything.
964	    ///
965	    /// All FOUR corners of the band are taken through `sourcePoint`, not the
966	    /// two the drag names: the band is axis-aligned in CANVAS space, so on a
967	    /// rotated layer its bounding box in Q is spanned by the other diagonal
968	    /// as much as by this one. At zero rotation the four collapse to the two
969	    /// and this is the rectangle that was dragged.
970	    func sourceRect(in box: CanvasLayerBox) -> CGRect? {
971	        let band = canvasRect
972	        guard didMove, band.width >= Self.minBand, band.height >= Self.minBand else { return nil }
973	        let corners = [
974	            CGPoint(x: band.minX, y: band.minY), CGPoint(x: band.maxX, y: band.minY),
975	            CGPoint(x: band.maxX, y: band.maxY), CGPoint(x: band.minX, y: band.maxY),
976	        ].map { box.sourcePoint($0) }
977	        guard let first = corners.first else { return nil }
978	        var minX = first.x, maxX = first.x, minY = first.y, maxY = first.y
979	        for point in corners.dropFirst() {
980	            minX = min(minX, point.x)
981	            maxX = max(maxX, point.x)
982	            minY = min(minY, point.y)
983	            maxY = max(maxY, point.y)
984	        }
985	        let rect = CGRect(x: minX, y: minY, width: maxX - minX, height: maxY - minY)
986	        guard rect.width > 0, rect.height > 0 else { return nil }
987	        return rect
988	    }
989	
990	    /// The band as the op's region: the CENTRE and the size, in source
991	    /// pixels from the cropped rect's centre. Rounded the way every canvas
992	    /// gesture rounds what it writes.
993	    ///
994	    /// `ZoomRegion` is `add_zoom_action`'s argument type
995	    /// (`ReelCore.swift`), and it is what an `ObscureProps` is built from
996	    /// too: the two commits differ in where the four numbers go, never in
997	    /// what they mean. The centre is taken before the rounding rather than
998	    /// after, so a band rounded to whole pixels cannot drift half a pixel
999	    /// off the rectangle that was drawn.
1000	    func region(in box: CanvasLayerBox) -> ZoomRegion? {
1001	        guard let rect = sourceRect(in: box) else { return nil }
1002	        return ZoomRegion(
1003	            x: canvasRound(rect.midX), y: canvasRound(rect.midY),
1004	            width: canvasRound(rect.width), height: canvasRound(rect.height))
1005	    }
1006	
1007	    /// The scale `add_zoom_action` will resolve for this band — `k = |cos θ|`,
1008	    /// `m = |sin θ|`, and the two formulas `edit_zoom.rs`'s module doc
1009	    /// derives, clamped into the layer's legal range exactly as the core
1010	    /// clamps before it computes the offsets.
1011	    ///
1012	    /// **This is a PREVIEW, and the core remains the authority.** Nothing is
1013	    /// written from it: the op recomputes the same number from the same
1014	    /// region, so the picture the band promises is the picture the op
1015	    /// produces. It is repeated here for one reason — a `fit`/`fill`
1016	    /// argument only means something if the band can differ from the result,
1017	    /// and the only way to show that difference is to draw it. If the two
1018	    /// ever disagree, `edit_zoom.rs` is right and this is the copy to fix.
1019	    func resolvedScale(in box: CanvasLayerBox, source: CGRect) -> Double {
1020	        let canvas = box.canvas.size
1021	        let radians = box.rotation * .pi / 180
1022	        let k = abs(cos(radians))
1023	        let m = abs(sin(radians))
1024	        let width = Double(canvas.width)
1025	        let height = Double(canvas.height)
1026	        let rw = Double(source.width)
1027	        let rh = Double(source.height)
1028	        let scale: Double
1029	        if fill {
1030	            scale = max((width * k + height * m) / rw, (width * m + height * k) / rh)
1031	        } else {
1032	            scale = min(width / (rw * k + rh * m), height / (rw * m + rh * k))
1033	        }
1034	        return min(max(scale, CanvasScaleSession.minScale), CanvasScaleSession.maxScale)
1035	    }
1036	
1037	    /// What the canvas will actually SHOW once the zoom lands, drawn in
1038	    /// today's canvas space.
1039	    ///
1040	    /// The derivation is two lines. After the zoom a point `q` sits at
1041	    /// `(W/2, H/2) + s′·R(θ)·(q − q_c)`, so the `q` still on screen are
1042	    /// `q_c + R(−θ)·u/s′` for `u` in the canvas box. Today that same set
1043	    /// draws at `canvasPoint(q_c) + (s/s′)·u`, because the two rotations
1044	    /// cancel: a zoom changes the layer's scale and position, never its
1045	    /// angle, so the rectangle is AXIS-ALIGNED in canvas space however the
1046	    /// layer is turned. It is centred on the region's centre and measures
1047	    /// `(s/s′)` of the canvas. For `fit` it is the smallest canvas-shaped
1048	    /// rectangle containing the region, and it touches it on one axis; for
1049	    /// `fill` it sits inside it. When the scale had to be clamped it grows,
1050	    /// which is the honest picture of a region too small to reach.
1051	    func frameRect(in box: CanvasLayerBox, source: CGRect) -> CGRect? {
1052	        guard purpose == .zoom else { return nil }
1053	        let resolved = resolvedScale(in: box, source: source)
1054	        let scale = box.video.scale > 0 ? box.video.scale : 1
1055	        guard resolved > 0 else { return nil }
1056	        let factor = CGFloat(scale / resolved)
1057	        let size = box.canvas.size
1058	        let centre = box.canvasPoint(source: CGPoint(x: source.midX, y: source.midY))
1059	        let width = size.width * factor
1060	        let height = size.height * factor
1061	        return CGRect(
1062	            x: centre.x - width / 2, y: centre.y - height / 2, width: width, height: height)
1063	    }
1064	}
1065	
1066	// MARK: - Pan
1067	
1068	/// Space-drag panning when the canvas is larger than the pane (spec §4.2).
1069	/// Pure view state: it never reaches the document.
1070	struct CanvasPanSession {
1071	    /// Pointer at mouse-down, VIEW points — the one session that works in
1072	    /// points, because panning is a property of the viewport and not of the
1073	    /// canvas.
1074	    let origin: CGPoint
1075	    let base: CGPoint
1076	    var offset: CGPoint
1077	
1078	    mutating func update(point: CGPoint) {
1079	        offset = CGPoint(x: base.x + (point.x - origin.x), y: base.y + (point.y - origin.y))
1080	    }
1081	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);

- `GraphicStore.swift` — one document's `graphics/` (road map 10 §5f):
  where it is (`<package>/graphics`, or an untitled document's
  `<NSTemporaryDirectory()>/FrameJob/<UUID>-graphics`, re-pointed by
  `packageDidMove(to:)` from the `fileURL` setter, posting
  `.graphicsLocationDidChange`), the scan (each legal `*.js` with its
  SHA-256 revision, G-13; `fonts/` validated on a throwaway
  `GraphicLibrary` once per file identity — size, modification date and
  file number — in `GraphicStore+Fonts.swift`'s `validatedFonts`, whose
  `fontVerdicts` is queue-confined and survives `stop()`/`start()` (spec
  §11 G-23 (f)); `assets/` with a 0-byte file, or a name `asset(name)`
  cannot use, warned and skipped, G-23 (e)) and the watch. **`graphics/` is created on the app's first write, never at
  open** (G-14): `ensureFolder()` is the ONE creator inside a package, and
  every app-side writer goes through `write(name:source:)` or it. While the
  folder is absent the store watches the PACKAGE directory, and the first
  observed appearance calls `folderDidAppear` →
  `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` once — without it the next save is
  refused as "changed by another application". A folder source raises
  `.write` only and an in-place save raises nothing on it (G0 q7), so each
  module, font and asset file has its own source, up to `fileSourceLimit` (16
  a pass, modules first, then fonts, then assets, each in name order; spec §11
  G-19 (c), G-20 (a)); a source whose `open` fails is a scan warning,
  "`<subject>` is not watched: open failed (`<strerror>`)", `errno` copied
  first (G-20 (b); `GraphicScan.warnings`, shown by the Source section and `get_graphic {}`,
  G-24 (b));
  every pass re-opens every source BY PATH and
  arms BEFORE it scans; events coalesce over 100 ms. The queue owns the diff
  and an outbox; main publishes in order through `drain()` (`scan`, the
  callback, `.graphicsDidChange` with sorted names — every module and
  `library: true` when the font/asset set moved; with NO names when the
  folder holds no module and only the library moved, which still posts, G5b).
  `GraphicStore+Files.swift` holds the store's own writes:
  `uniqueModuleName(_:)`, the one free-name rule (`-copy`, `-copy-N`)
  Duplicate and Insert ▸ Graphic share, which takes a name as held when the
  scan OR the disk has it (`holdsModule(named:)`, #75); `write(name:source:)`
  and `importFile` land through `land(at:writing:)`, whose `.partial` is
  removed on any failure; and `removeScratchRoot()`, which removes an untitled
  root after `stop()` — from `packageDidMove(to:)` and `stopGraphicStore()`
  (G-19 (d)). It also holds the app's delete and rename, each inside
  `onQueue` (main only, never on the store's queue) so no pass runs between
  their steps: `removeModule(named:)` keeps the file's bytes and then removes
  it, refusing when the text could not be kept, and `moveModule(from:to:)`
  moves the file, journals the pair and reads it back — a rename that cannot
  be journalled is refused — and then moves its history, a throw leaving the
  file and the history where they were and the journal put back as it was
  read (its bytes, or no file: `renameJournalBytes` / `putBackRenameJournal`
  in `GraphicStore+History.swift`), so a refused rename journals no pair; a
  crash between the three steps is G-28 (f)'s limit; neither rescans.
  `write(name:bytes:)` is `write(name:source:)` for bytes as they are, and
  `noModuleSentence(_:)` the one sentence for an absent module.
  `GraphicStore+History.swift` is the kept revisions and the rename journal
  (spec §11 G-27..G-29): `graphics/history/<name>/<%06d sequence>-<revision>.js`,
  the last `historyLimit` (10) per module, and `history/renames.json`, at
  most `renameJournalLimit` (32) pairs. `keepReplaced`, called by `pass` on
  the queue before it stores its scan, keeps the bytes a module's new text
  replaced and drops the new text's own revision, so history never holds the
  current text; nothing is kept at `start()` or for a removal the app did not
  make, and `start()` drops each module's current revision from its history.
  `history/` is created only inside an existing `graphics/` (G-14) with no
  `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` call, and `moveHistory` leaves no
  `history/<from>/` behind — which is what makes 'no file, something kept'
  mean a DELETED module. `GraphicStore+Import.swift`'s `importAsset` files a name
  `asset(name)` cannot use under `GraphicAssetName.legalized`, a renamed
  copy taking `-2`, `-3`, … while `holdsAsset(named:)` (scan or disk) says
  the name is held, and answers `name`/`renamedFrom` (G-23 (c), (d)).
  `landNew` is the `.fjgraphic` import's write (G-47 (e)): bytes landed
  under a name not yet taken, never replacing a file. **`drain()` is not
  re-entrant: never call `rescan()` from a `.graphicsDidChange` observer.**
  `stop()` bumps a generation under `queue.sync`. `makeLibrary()` is a NEW
  builder every call (a library freezes on first use). It also writes the
  app's bundled reference into an EXISTING folder as `API.md` and `API.d.ts`
  (`writeManual()`, from `start()` for a saved package, `ensureFolder()` and
  `write()`; only when the bytes differ) — never a reason to create the
  folder (G-14).

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is

traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

2	title: "The canvas"
3	description: "What the preview's canvas shows, how clips stack on it, and what you can do directly on the picture."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
8	
9	The canvas is the fixed frame every clip is drawn into. It's where you place a clip's picture, and every export starts from it.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  where={['The preview pane', 'Document tab, for its size, rate and background']}
13	  tools={['render_frame', 'set_video', 'set_selection']}
14	/>
15	
16	<Shot
17	  name="04-editor.window"
18	  alt="The editor with nothing selected. In the preview pane a black 960 × 540 canvas sits in a grey surround, showing a navy video clip smaller than the frame, the words Frame Job inside a white ellipse in front of it, and a lower-third title at the bottom left. The caption under the picture reads 960 × 540 · 30 fps."
19	/>
20	
21	## What the canvas shows
22	
23	The canvas shows the composition at the playhead, at the project's size, centred in the preview pane with a margin of 24 points round it. A thin line marks its edge, so a black canvas still shows against the area around it.
24	
25	A clip smaller than the canvas leaves whatever is behind it showing, down to the background colour. A clip larger than the canvas is cut off at its edge.
26	
27	You don't set the canvas up here. Its size is on [Canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/), and its rate and background colour are on the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/).
28	
29	## The caption
30	
31	The small line under the picture states the canvas size and frame rate, for example `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps`.
32	
33	## Layers
34	
35	Tracks stack back to front, so a track higher in the timeline draws in front of the ones below it. A track doesn't hold one kind of clip: video, image, still, text, shape, graphic and nest clips can share a track, and you place them all with the same gestures and the same Picture sections, apart from the exceptions on their own pages.
36	
37	An adjustment clip has no picture of its own, so it has no box on the canvas. Select it on the timeline. See [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/).
38	
39	## Working on the canvas
40	
41	Drag on the picture and the placement changes. The [Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/) shows the same placement as numbers.
42	
43	| To | Do this | More |
44	| --- | --- | --- |
45	| Select a clip | Click it. | [Select on the canvas](/canvas/select-on-canvas/) |
46	| Move a clip | Drag inside its box. | [Move](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/#move) |
47	| Resize a clip | Drag one of the eight square handles. | [Scale](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/#scale) |
48	| Rotate a clip | Drag the round grip above the top edge. | [Rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/#rotate) |
49	| Crop a clip | Press <kbd>C</kbd>, or double-click a clip that isn't text. | [Crop](/canvas/crop/) |
50	| Change a title's words | Double-click a text clip. | [Edit text on the canvas](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/) |
51	| Move one end of a line or arrow | Drag its round end handle. | [Lines and arrows](/text-and-shapes/lines-and-arrows/) |
52	
53	Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> during a drag to [cancel it](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/#cancel-a-drag).
54	
55	### With an action selected
56	
57	While an action is selected on the clip, a move, scale, rotate or crop drag changes that action's end state, as the inspector's fields do. The box on screen still shows the frame at the playhead. See [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/).
58	
59	Two things always change the clip itself: resizing a shape's box and dragging a line's end. Several clips selected at once have no selected action, so a drag on them changes the clips too.
60	
61	## Hidden and locked tracks
62	
63	Clips on a hidden track aren't drawn, so you can't click them. A clip with its [picture turned off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/) draws nothing either, and can't be clicked.
64	
65	Clips on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) are drawn, but you can't select or move them on the canvas. A click passes through to whatever is behind.
66	
67	- A locked clip you select on the timeline shows its outline on the canvas, with no handles.
68	- If the front-most selected clip is locked, nothing gets handles, even when an unlocked clip is selected behind it.
69	- A drag of several clips leaves any on a locked track where they are.
70	
71	## Canvas modes
72	
73	Some tools wait for a click or a drag on the picture. While one is armed the pointer is a crosshair, a hint pill at the top of the preview says what to do, and the canvas takes every press.
74	
75	| Mode | Arm it with | The hint reads |
76	| --- | --- | --- |
77	| [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) | <kbd>Z</kbd>, or the Zoom to Region button above the action lane | "Drag a rectangle to zoom to it · ⇧ fills · Esc to cancel" |
78	| [Place on Canvas](/effects/obscure/) | **Place on Canvas** in the Obscure section | "Drag a rectangle to obscure · Esc to cancel" |
79	| [Pick from Canvas](/effects/chroma-key/), for a chroma key | **Pick from Canvas** in the Chroma Key section | "Click to pick the key color · Esc to cancel" |
80	| [Pick from Canvas](/color/pick-from-canvas/), for a qualifier | **Pick from Canvas** in the Qualifier section | "Click to pick the colour to qualify · Esc to cancel" |
81	
82	Only one mode can be armed at a time, and arming one ends the other. A mode ends when:
83	
84	- you finish the drag or the pick
85	- you press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, which changes nothing
86	- you press its key or button a second time
87	- the selection changes so that it's no longer aimed at the same clips
88	
89	Zoom to Region and Place on Canvas need exactly one selected clip that's drawing at the playhead and isn't on a locked track. Otherwise Frame Job beeps and the mode doesn't start. The two pick modes beep the same way when nothing selected can use them. A pick that lands outside the canvas beeps and the mode stays armed.
90	
91	## With an agent
92	
93	`render_frame` writes the frame at a moment as a picture file, through the same path an export takes, so an agent can look at what it made. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).

1	---
2	title: "Zoom and pan the preview"
3	description: "Look closer at the picture with the zoom popup, the View menu or a pinch, and move around a canvas bigger than the pane."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	Zoom the preview to look closely at the picture or to place something precisely, then pan to reach the part you want. Zooming is only a way of looking: it changes nothing in the project, makes no undo step and is never exported.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['View ▸ Zoom In', 'View ▸ Zoom Out', 'View ▸ Zoom to Fit']}
12	  keys={['⌘+', '⌘=', '⌘-', '⌘0']}
13	  where={['The zoom popup in the toolbar', 'Pinch, ⌥-scroll or ⌘-scroll over the preview', 'Scroll or Space-drag to pan']}
14	/>
15	
16	## The zoom popup
17	
18	The popup in the toolbar sets how large the picture appears. Its stops are **Fit**, **50%**, **100%** and **200%**. It always shows the zoom the canvas is at, however you got there.
19	
20	**Fit** sizes the canvas to the pane and follows the pane as it changes. At **100%**, one canvas pixel takes one point on screen.
21	
22	Each window starts at **Fit**, and the zoom isn't saved with the project.
23	
24	## View menu commands
25	
26	| Command | Key | What it does |
27	| --- | --- | --- |
28	| **View ▸ Zoom In** | <kbd>⌘+</kbd> or <kbd>⌘=</kbd> | Goes to the next stop up. Greyed at 200%. |
29	| **View ▸ Zoom Out** | <kbd>⌘-</kbd> | Goes to the next stop down. Greyed at Fit. |
30	| **View ▸ Zoom to Fit** | <kbd>⌘0</kbd> | Goes straight back to Fit and centres the canvas. Greyed at Fit. |
31	
32	These zoom the preview. To zoom the timeline, see [Zoom and scroll the timeline](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/).
33	
34	## Pinch and scroll
35	
36	Pinch on a trackpad over the preview, or scroll with <kbd>⌥</kbd> or <kbd>⌘</kbd> held, to step through the same four stops. The stops are separate steps, so a gesture has to build up a little before it takes the next one.
37	
38	## Panning
39	
40	When the zoomed canvas is bigger than the pane, there are two ways to move it:
41	
42	- Scroll over the preview.
43	- Hold <kbd>Space</kbd> and drag. Click the canvas first if it doesn't have focus, because the canvas has to be holding the keyboard for <kbd>Space</kbd> to reach it.
44	
45	A pan only works along a side where the canvas overflows the pane, so you can't drag the canvas out of view. While the canvas fits, a plain scroll does nothing.
46	
47	Moving between stops keeps your pan, pulled back if it no longer fits. Going back to **Fit** centres the canvas again.
48	
49	## Space on the canvas
50	
51	With the canvas focused, <kbd>Space</kbd> still plays and pauses. Frame Job can't tell a tap from a pan until you let go, so playback starts or stops on the release rather than the press. If you panned while <kbd>Space</kbd> was down, the release does nothing to playback.
52	
53	## Good to know
54	
55	- The stops count up from **Fit** in order, whatever size Fit happens to be. On a small canvas in a large pane, **50%** can be smaller than **Fit**.
56	- While the canvas fits, holding <kbd>Space</kbd> and dragging a clip moves the clip as usual, and playback toggles when you let go of <kbd>Space</kbd>.

1	---
2	title: "Select on the canvas"
3	description: "Pick clips by clicking them in the preview, add to or clear the selection, and read the frame and handles a selected clip gets."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
8	
9	Click a clip in the preview to work on it there, without hunting for it on the timeline. It's the same selection the timeline and the inspector use.
10	
11	<AtAGlance keys="⇧-click" where="The preview canvas" tools="set_selection" />
12	
13	<Shot
14	  name="05-clip-picture.window"
15	  alt="A video clip selected in the editor. In the preview it has a thin coral outline with white square handles at its four corners and the middle of its four edges, and a round grip on a short stalk above its top edge. The inspector's Clip tab shows the clip's Picture sub-tab."
16	/>
17	
18	## Click a layer
19	
20	Click the picture to select the front-most visible clip under the pointer at the playhead. The test follows the layer's rotation, so a turned clip is selected by the shape you can see, not by the box it would have upright.
21	
22	The selected clip's handles come first: a handle lying on top of another clip still grabs the handle, so you can resize a clip that has others in front of it.
23	
24	Clicking a clip that's already part of a multiple selection keeps the whole selection, so you can drag them together. To narrow it down to one clip, click empty canvas first or use the [timeline](/timeline/selecting-clips/).
25	
26	## Shift-click
27	
28	<kbd>⇧</kbd>-click adds a clip to the selection, or takes it out if it's already selected.
29	
30	## Click the void
31	
32	Click empty canvas, or the area around it, to clear the selection. This also leaves [crop mode](/canvas/crop/).
33	
34	With <kbd>⇧</kbd> held the selection stays, and crop mode still ends.
35	
36	## The selection frame
37	
38	Every selected clip that's drawing at the playhead gets a coral outline with a dark backing line, so it shows on both light and dark pictures. The front-most selected clip has a heavier outline and carries the handles:
39	
40	- Eight white square handles, at the corners and the middle of each edge, for [scaling](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/#scale).
41	- A round grip on a stalk above the top edge, for [rotating](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/#rotate).
42	- On a [line or arrow](/text-and-shapes/lines-and-arrows/), a round handle at each end as well.
43	
44	The handles stay the same size on screen at every zoom. The pointer shows what a handle does: a left-right or up-down resize pointer on an edge handle, and a crosshair on a corner.
45	
46	A selected clip that isn't at the playhead has no frame, because it isn't in the picture. An adjustment clip never has one, because it has no rectangle of its own.
47	
48	## Matte clips
49	
50	A clip on a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) can be selected and dragged inside its own box, even though it draws nothing there.
51	
52	Because it's the front-most clip inside that box, a click there selects the matte clip. To select the clip it cuts, click outside the matte clip's box, or use the timeline.
53	
54	## Good to know
55	
56	Clips on hidden tracks can't be clicked, and clips on locked tracks are passed over. See [Hidden and locked tracks](/canvas/the-canvas/#hidden-and-locked-tracks).
57
