270	/// The mode's view: a transparent sheet over the whole canvas pane that takes
271	/// one drag, draws it, wears the crosshair, and says how to get back out.
272	///
273	/// It holds the purpose, the clip and the live session, and nothing else.
274	/// Where the band landed on the canvas, what the layer under it looks like,
275	/// and what to do about it are all the view controller's — the same division
276	/// `CanvasOverlayView` keeps with `PreviewCanvasView`, and the reason the
277	/// five closures below take and answer plain points and rectangles.
278	final class CanvasRegionView: CanvasModeOverlay {
279	    /// What the band is for. Read here only for the hint pill; the commit
280	    /// branches on the session's copy.
281	    let purpose: CanvasRegionPurpose
282	    /// The clip the mode was armed for.
283	    let clip: UInt32
284	    /// A second hint pill under the first; nil draws none. A `var` because
285	    /// what it says is a fact about the CLIP, which can change while the mode
286	    /// is armed — `syncRegionMode` re-reads it on every `refreshCanvas`.
287	    var note: String? {
288	        didSet {
289	            if note != oldValue { needsDisplay = true }
290	        }
291	    }
292	    /// Live between mouse-down and mouse-up, and nil either side of it.
293	    private(set) var session: ZoomRegionSession?
294	
295	    /// A WINDOW point as canvas pixels; nil when there is no canvas to ask.
296	    var canvasPoint: ((CGPoint) -> CGPoint?)?
297	    /// A canvas point in this view's own coordinates.
298	    var viewPoint: ((CGPoint) -> CGPoint)?
299	    /// The rectangle the zoom will frame, in canvas pixels.
300	    var resolvedFrame: ((ZoomRegionSession) -> CGRect?)?
301	    var onCommit: ((ZoomRegionSession) -> Void)?
302	
303	    private static let zoomHint = "Drag a rectangle to zoom to it · ⇧ fills · Esc to cancel"
304	    private static let obscureHint = "Drag a rectangle to obscure · Esc to cancel"
305	    static let duringNote = "This clip has During motion — the zoom is solved without it"
306	    /// The band's own stroke, and the resolved frame's at a lower alpha —
307	    /// the same ink, because they are two readings of one rectangle.
308	    private static let frameAlpha: CGFloat = 0.45
309	
310	    init(purpose: CanvasRegionPurpose, clip: UInt32, note: String? = nil) {
311	        self.purpose = purpose
312	        self.clip = clip
313	        self.note = note
314	        super.init(frame: .zero)
315	    }
316	
317	    @available(*, unavailable)
318	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
319	        fatalError("CanvasRegionView does not support NSCoder")
320	    }
321	
322	    // MARK: Events
323	
324	    /// The press starts the band wherever it landed — including in the void
325	    /// around the picture. A region's centre is allowed outside the layer
326	    /// (the core asks only that x and y be finite), and dragging in from the
327	    /// margin to catch the edge of the frame is the ordinary way to do it.
328	    override func mouseDown(with event: NSEvent) {
329	        guard let point = canvasPoint?(event.locationInWindow) else {
330	            NSSound.beep()
331	            return
332	        }
333	        session = ZoomRegionSession(
334	            purpose: purpose, clip: clip, anchor: point, current: point,
335	            fill: event.modifierFlags.contains(.shift))
336	        needsDisplay = true
337	    }
338	
339	    override func mouseDragged(with event: NSEvent) {
340	        track(event)
341	    }
342	
343	    /// The release tears this view down from inside this very call — the same
344	    /// shape as the eyedropper's pick — so the last reference to it must not
345	    /// be the superview's.
346	    override func mouseUp(with event: NSEvent) {
347	        track(event)
348	        guard let finished = session else { return }
349	        session = nil
350	        withExtendedLifetime(self) { onCommit?(finished) }
351	    }
352	
353	    /// ⇧ is read at every step rather than latched at the press, so the
354	    /// choice between fit and fill can be made while the band is being drawn
355	    /// and the resolved frame answers it as it is made.
356	    private func track(_ event: NSEvent) {
357	        guard var live = session, let point = canvasPoint?(event.locationInWindow) else { return }
358	        live.update(point: point, fill: event.modifierFlags.contains(.shift))
359	        session = live
360	        needsDisplay = true
361	    }
362	
363	    /// Esc drops a band in progress BEFORE the base runs `onCancel`, so the
364	    /// mode never ends with a live session on it.
365	    override func keyDown(with event: NSEvent) {
366	        if event.keyCode == 53 { session = nil }
367	        super.keyDown(with: event)
368	    }
369	
370	    override func detachCallbacks() {
371	        canvasPoint = nil
372	        viewPoint = nil
373	        resolvedFrame = nil
374	        onCommit = nil
375	        super.detachCallbacks()
376	    }
377	
378	    // MARK: Drawing
379	
380	    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
381	        drawBand()
382	        drawHint()
383	    }
384	
385	    /// The band, and — for a zoom — the rectangle it resolves to.
386	    ///
387	    /// Both are AXIS-ALIGNED in canvas space (the band by construction, the
388	    /// frame because a zoom changes a layer's scale and position and never
389	    /// its angle), and the canvas-to-view mapping is a scale and a
390	    /// translation, so two converted corners describe each of them. Nothing
391	    /// here is rotated, which is why the marquee's flat rectangle is honest
392	    /// even over a turned clip.
393	    private func drawBand() {
394	        guard let session = session, let convert = viewPoint else { return }
395	        let band = rect(from: convert(session.anchor), to: convert(session.current))
396	        guard band.width >= 1, band.height >= 1 else { return }
397	        let path = NSBezierPath(rect: band.insetBy(dx: 0.5, dy: 0.5))
398	        DS.selectionFill.setFill()
399	        path.fill()
400	        DS.marquee.setStroke()
401	        path.stroke()
402	
403	        guard let canvasFrame = resolvedFrame?(session) else { return }
404	        let frame = rect(
405	            from: convert(CGPoint(x: canvasFrame.minX, y: canvasFrame.minY)),
406	            to: convert(CGPoint(x: canvasFrame.maxX, y: canvasFrame.maxY)))
407	        guard frame.width >= 1, frame.height >= 1 else { return }
408	        let ghost = NSBezierPath(rect: frame.insetBy(dx: 0.5, dy: 0.5))
409	        // Dashed as well as dimmed: the two rectangles coincide on one axis
410	        // under `fit`, and a solid stroke at a lower alpha under a solid one
411	        // reads as a rendering artefact rather than as a second rectangle.
412	        let dash: [CGFloat] = [4, 3]
413	        ghost.setLineDash(dash, count: dash.count, phase: 0)
414	        DS.marquee.withAlphaComponent(Self.frameAlpha).setStroke()
415	        ghost.stroke()
416	    }

418	    private func rect(from a: CGPoint, to b: CGPoint) -> CGRect {
419	        CGRect(
420	            x: min(a.x, b.x), y: min(a.y, b.y), width: abs(b.x - a.x), height: abs(b.y - a.y))
421	    }

423	    /// The mode's hint, and the During note under it: two of the base's
424	    /// pills (`drawPill`), so every canvas mode announces itself the same way.
425	    private func drawHint() {
426	        let hint = purpose == .zoom ? Self.zoomHint : Self.obscureHint
427	        let height = drawPill(hint, top: Self.hintTop)
428	        // 6 pt between the two pills: a gap that reads as two lines of one hint.
429	        if let note = note { _ = drawPill(note, top: Self.hintTop + height + 6) }

3	/// The editor's document window, and the two things it decides: where a bare
4	/// Space goes (spec §11 K-1, kpgalligan/framejob#35), and when text gives
5	/// the keys back (K-4, `TextFocus` below), which it asks first.
6	///
7	/// **Space is the transport's unless the first responder is typing or claims
8	/// it.** The window routes a bare Space key-DOWN (⇧ and ⇪ allowed, any other
9	/// modifier untouched) BEFORE dispatch, because dispatch is what beeped when
10	/// the WINDOW was first responder — as it still can be when a focused view is
11	/// removed (`OptionFieldControl.finishEditing` hands focus to the content
12	/// view since #60): `NSWindow.keyDown` forwards to nothing, and
13	/// `NSResponder.noResponder(for:)` beeps — the key never reached
14	/// `EditorViewController.keyDown`.
15	///
16	/// Three claimants keep the key:
17	/// - an editable `NSTextView` — every field editor, the Text tab's area, the
18	///   canvas's inline editor, the Media tab's search field — so a Space is
19	///   TYPED there;
20	/// - an `NSButton` (which covers `NSPopUpButton`) or an `NSSegmentedControl`:
21	///   they press on Space by AppKit's own convention, reachable only under
22	///   Full Keyboard Access, and an accessibility user keeps it;
23	/// - the canvas overlay (`CanvasOverlayView`), whose own Space arms a pan and
24	///   toggles play on key-UP (`PreviewCanvasView.handleKeyUp`).
25	/// And nothing is taken while a sheet is attached. An auto-repeat of a Space
26	/// the window took is swallowed. A non-editable field editor (a selectable
27	/// label), a slider, the window itself and every custom inspector control
28	/// are the transport's.
29	///
30	/// `handleEditorCharacter`'s `case " "` in `EditorViewController` stays for
31	/// the preview panel's forward (`PreviewWindowController.keyDown`) and is
32	/// dead for this window.
33	enum SpaceKeyRoute: Equatable { case transport, held, responder }
34	
35	enum SpaceKey {
36	    /// nil unless `event` is a key-DOWN of keyCode 49 whose device-independent
37	    /// flags ⊆ [.shift, .capsLock]. Pure: reads only its arguments.
38	    static func route(
39	        _ event: NSEvent, firstResponder: NSResponder?, sheetAttached: Bool
40	    ) -> SpaceKeyRoute? {
41	        guard event.type == .keyDown, event.keyCode == 49 else { return nil }
42	        let flags = event.modifierFlags.intersection(.deviceIndependentFlagsMask)
43	        guard flags.subtracting([.shift, .capsLock]).isEmpty else { return nil }
44	        if sheetAttached { return .responder }
45	        if (firstResponder as? NSTextView)?.isEditable == true { return .responder }
46	        if firstResponder is NSButton || firstResponder is NSSegmentedControl
47	            || firstResponder is CanvasOverlayView
48	        {
49	            return .responder
50	        }
51	        if event.isARepeat { return .held }
52	        return .transport
53	    }
54	}

56	/// When the editor window takes the keys back from text (spec §11 K-4):
57	/// typing is focus-averse. Only a click, or a command that exists to type,
58	/// gives text the keys; a click outside it, Tab (unless Full Keyboard Access
59	/// is on), and Return in a one-line field hand them back to the content
60	/// view — the root that holds the bare-key map — BEFORE dispatch, so Space
61	/// plays the moment typing ends.
62	///
63	/// Before dispatch because of what dispatch did: a click on the timeline,
64	/// which refuses first responder, left the field editor attached, and
65	/// AppKit's own Return re-selected the field after its commit — both behind
66	/// no focus ring, so the next Space was typed into a field that looked left.
67	/// Each field still commits through its own end-of-editing path, as on any
68	/// blur. Pure, so a probe can ask it.
69	enum TextFocus {
70	    /// The text taking keys when `responder` is editable text — every field
71	    /// editor, the Text tab's area, the canvas's inline editor, the
72	    /// composer — else nil.
73	    static func typing(_ responder: NSResponder?) -> NSTextView? {
74	        guard let text = responder as? NSTextView, text.isEditable else { return nil }
75	        return text
76	    }
77	
78	    /// Where a click keeps the typing: a field editor's field, or the
79	    /// `OptionFieldControl` that frames it (its margins and chevron are the
80	    /// field's own); else the text view's scroll view, so a scroller is
81	    /// inside; else the text view.
82	    static func host(of text: NSTextView) -> NSView {
83	        if text.isFieldEditor, let field = text.delegate as? NSView {
84	            return (field.superview as? OptionFieldControl) ?? field
85	        }
86	        return text.enclosingScrollView ?? text
87	    }
88	
89	    /// True when the key-down `event` leaves `text`: Tab or ⇧Tab in any
90	    /// text, unless `fullKeyboardAccess` — then Tab is AppKit's key-view
91	    /// loop, how such a user reaches a control (K-1's exception); Return or
92	    /// keypad Enter in a field editor (⇧ ⇪, and the keypad and fn flags,
93	    /// allowed). ⌃Tab, ⌥Return and ⌘ are AppKit's; a multi-line view routes
94	    /// its own Return (`TextEditKey`). Never while an input method has
95	    /// marked text.
96	    static func leavesOnKey(
97	        _ event: NSEvent, in text: NSTextView, fullKeyboardAccess: Bool
98	    ) -> Bool {
99	        guard event.type == .keyDown, !text.hasMarkedText() else { return false }
100	        let flags = event.modifierFlags.intersection(.deviceIndependentFlagsMask)
101	        switch event.keyCode {
102	        case 48:
103	            return !fullKeyboardAccess && flags.subtracting([.shift, .capsLock]).isEmpty
104	        case 36, 76:
105	            return text.isFieldEditor
106	                && flags.subtracting([.shift, .capsLock, .numericPad, .function]).isEmpty
107	        default:
108	            return false
109	        }
110	    }
111	
112	    /// True when a mouse-down whose content hit is `hit` leaves `text`: a
113	    /// hit outside its host. nil — the click is outside the content view,
114	    /// on the title bar — never leaves.
115	    static func leavesOnClick(hit: NSView?, in text: NSTextView) -> Bool {
116	        guard let hit else { return false }
117	        return !hit.isDescendant(of: host(of: text))
118	    }
119	}

121	/// The bare-key map's modifier rule, read by `handleEditorKey` (#61).
122	enum EditorKey {
123	    /// Device-independent part of `flags` minus [.shift, .capsLock] must be empty, except that on a
124	    /// function-key scalar (0xF700...0xF8FF) .numericPad and .function are also allowed. ⌘ ⌥ ⌃ .help never. Pure.
125	    static func isBare(_ flags: NSEvent.ModifierFlags, scalar: UInt32) -> Bool {
126	        var allowed: NSEvent.ModifierFlags = [.shift, .capsLock]
127	        if (0xF700...0xF8FF).contains(scalar) { allowed.formUnion([.numericPad, .function]) }
128	        return flags.intersection(.deviceIndependentFlagsMask).subtracting(allowed).isEmpty
129	    }
130	}

151	        // A key that leaves is spent; a click that leaves is then delivered.
152	        if leaveText(for: event), event.type == .keyDown { return }
153	        switch SpaceKey.route(

169	    /// `TextFocus`'s rule applied: true when `event` left the text, first
170	    /// responder now the content view. A field that refuses to resign keeps
171	    /// the event, and nothing is taken while a sheet is attached.
172	    private func leaveText(for event: NSEvent) -> Bool {
173	        guard attachedSheet == nil, let text = TextFocus.typing(firstResponder),
174	              let content = contentView
175	        else { return false }
176	        let leaves: Bool
177	        switch event.type {

180	                event, in: text, fullKeyboardAccess: NSApp.isFullKeyboardAccessEnabled)

185	        default:
186	            leaves = false
187	        }
188	        return leaves && makeFirstResponder(content)
189	    }

721	        // `,`/`.` nudge, `i`/`o` write the range. A sheet captures a project
722	        // handle and reads it again later, so the document must not move
723	        // under it. Until phase 8b that held here for free and needed no line,
724	        // since a sheet takes the editor window's key status and this method
725	        // was simply unreachable while one was up. But a sheet is WINDOW-modal
726	        // rather than application-modal (measured: with one attached
727	        // `NSApp.modalWindow` is nil, and the preview panel is visible and
728	        // `canBecomeKey`), and the panel forwards its bare keys straight here,
729	        // where no validator stands — `t` added a text clip behind an open
730	        // export card that had already captured the project it was about to
731	        // write, and Remove Silences, which computes its spans ONCE, would
732	        // have rippled ranges that no longer described the timeline. The guard
733	        // belongs beside the key map rather than in the panel: both windows
734	        // inherit it, no second copy can drift, and the editor's own path pays
735	        // nothing for a case it cannot reach.
736	        if view.window?.attachedSheet != nil { return false }
737	        let flags = event.modifierFlags.intersection(.deviceIndependentFlagsMask)
738	        guard let scalar = event.charactersIgnoringModifiers?.unicodeScalars.first else {
739	            return false
740	        }
741	        guard EditorKey.isBare(flags, scalar: scalar.value) else { return false }
742	        let shift = flags.contains(.shift)
743	        switch scalar.value {
744	        case UInt32(NSLeftArrowFunctionKey):
745	            stepFrames(shift ? -10 : -1)
746	        case UInt32(NSRightArrowFunctionKey):
747	            stepFrames(shift ? 10 : 1)
748	        case UInt32(NSUpArrowFunctionKey):
749	            previousEditPoint(nil)
750	        case UInt32(NSDownArrowFunctionKey):
751	            nextEditPoint(nil)
752	        case UInt32(NSHomeFunctionKey):
753	            goToStart(nil)
754	        case UInt32(NSEndFunctionKey):
755	            goToEnd(nil)
756	        case 27: return deselectActionCommand()
757	        default:
758	            return handleEditorCharacter(Character(scalar), shift: shift)
759	        }
760	        return true
761	    }
762	
763	    /// Compared as a lowercased STRING, not a `Character`: lowercasing is not
764	    /// one-to-one in every locale (a Turkish "İ" becomes two scalars), and
765	    /// `Character(String)` traps on anything but exactly one.
766	    private func handleEditorCharacter(_ character: Character, shift: Bool) -> Bool {
767	        switch character.lowercased() {
768	        case " ":
769	            playPause(nil)
770	        case "j":
771	            shuttle(forward: false)
772	        case "k":
773	            playback.pause()
774	        case "l":
775	            shuttle(forward: true)
776	        case "i":
777	            setInPoint(nil)
778	        case "o":
779	            setOutPoint(nil)
780	        case "n":
781	            toggleSnapping(nil)
782	        case "m":
783	            addMarker(nil)
784	        case "w":
785	            trimStartToPlayhead(nil)
786	        case "e":
787	            trimEndToPlayhead(nil)
788	        case "t":
789	            addTextClip(nil)
790	        case "c":
791	            toggleCropMode(nil)
792	        case "z" where shift:
793	            fitTimeline(nil)
794	        // Bare Z arms the canvas region mode (road map 2's phase 3b, spec §9),
795	        // and it must stay BELOW the ⇧Z case: a `switch` matches in source
796	        // order, so a bare "z" above it would swallow Fit Timeline silently.
797	        // The command itself toggles, so Z is also the way back out
798	        // (EditorViewController+ZoomRegion.swift).
799	        case "z":
800	            zoomToRegion(nil)

802	        // as "<" on a US layout — both spellings mean the same nudge.
803	        case ",", "<":
804	            nudgeSelection(frames: shift ? -10 : -1)
805	        case ".", ">":
806	            nudgeSelection(frames: shift ? 10 : 1)
807	        default:
808	            return false
809	        }
810	        return true
811	    }

5	/// A view whose PRESENCE over the canvas pane IS a mode: the chroma
6	/// eyedropper's sheet (below) and the region band
7	/// (`EditorViewController+ZoomRegion.swift`). Each covers the whole picture,
8	/// swallows every click on it and holds first responder so Esc reaches it, so
9	/// **at most one may be armed at a time**.
10	///
11	/// Nothing else coordinates them: each is found by KIND among
12	/// `canvasContainer`'s subviews, and an extension has no stored state in which
13	/// either could see the other. So the rule lives in the one place both entry
14	/// points have to pass through anyway — `armCanvasMode`, the only code that
15	/// installs one of these views — and this protocol is what lets it end the
16	/// others without naming them. Every one of them is a `CanvasModeOverlay`
17	/// (below), which holds what they share — Esc, the crosshair, the hint pill,
18	/// `detachCallbacks` — and `dismissCanvasMode` is their one teardown.
19	protocol CanvasModalMode: NSView {}
20	
21	extension EditorViewController {
22	    /// Installs a modal canvas mode over the canvas pane and gives it the
23	    /// keyboard, ending whichever mode was armed before it.
24	    ///
25	    /// **Why ending the others is here and not at the call sites.** Arming one
26	    /// mode while another was armed used to leave BOTH overlays installed,
27	    /// stacked over the same pane: the lower one kept its callbacks, kept its
28	    /// `sync…` hook, and was still ready to commit its own edit from a gesture
29	    /// aimed at the upper one — which is how arming the eyedropper under an
30	    /// armed region band turned the next canvas drag into an unasked-for zoom
31	    /// action. One entry point remembered to end its sibling and the other did
32	    /// not; from here neither can forget, and a third mode inherits the rule by
33	    /// being installed at all.
34	    func armCanvasMode(_ mode: CanvasModalMode) {
35	        endCanvasModes()
36	        mode.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
37	        canvasContainer.addSubview(mode)
38	        // Over the PICTURE, not the pane: the scopes panel (GR-5) shares the
39	        // pane and must not be covered by a mode that swallows its clicks.
40	        let picture: NSView = previewCanvas ?? canvasContainer
41	        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
42	            mode.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: picture.topAnchor),
43	            mode.bottomAnchor.constraint(equalTo: picture.bottomAnchor),
44	            mode.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: picture.leadingAnchor),
45	            mode.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: picture.trailingAnchor),
46	        ])
47	        view.window?.makeFirstResponder(mode)
48	        view.window?.invalidateCursorRects(for: mode)
49	    }

51	    /// Ends every armed modal canvas mode. Each `end…` is a no-op when its own
52	    /// mode is not armed, so this is the whole cost of a new mode: one line.
53	    private func endCanvasModes() {
54	        endChromaEyedropper()
55	        endQualifierPick()
56	        endRegionMode()
57	    }

59	    /// Tears one armed mode down: every `end…` is this with its own mode. A
60	    /// no-op for nil, which is "that mode is not armed".
61	    func dismissCanvasMode(_ mode: CanvasModeOverlay?) {
62	        guard let mode else { return }
63	        // The pitfall `PreviewCanvasView.finishTextEditing` documents: the
64	        // teardown runs from inside the overlay's OWN event handler, so the
65	        // callbacks are cleared before the view goes and a second entry finds
66	        // nothing to do instead of recursing.
67	        mode.detachCallbacks()
68	        mode.removeFromSuperview()
69	        // The crosshair belonged to a view that is now gone; without this the
70	        // pointer keeps it until the next mouse-moved event lands somewhere
71	        // with a cursor rect of its own.

225	            let reading = snapshot.output == .hlg
226	                ? KeyReading.common(keyed.map { KeyReading.of(media: $0, url: urls[$0.id]) })
227	                : .unlift
228	            let frame = Exporter.renderFrame(
229	                project: project, urls: urls, at: time, maxWidth: nil, graphics: graphics)
230	            let picked = frame.flatMap {
231	                CanvasEyedropperSession.keyColor(
232	                    at: target, in: $0, canvas: snapshot, reading: reading)
233	            }
234	            DispatchQueue.main.async { self?.chromaKeySampled(picked, session: session) }
235	        }
236	    }
237	
238	    /// Back on the main thread with the sampled colour.
239	    ///
240	    /// The commit goes through the BINDING rather than straight to the
241	    /// document, because the binding is the one place that knows an edit made
242	    /// while the playhead sits inside an action belongs to that action's end
243	    /// state rather than to the clip's base props (§4.3) — and `applyGrouped`
244	    /// is its off-event door, which this is.
245	    private func chromaKeySampled(_ color: RGBA?, session: CanvasEyedropperSession) {
246	        guard let inspector = inspector, let color = color else {
247	            // A frame that would not compose, or a pixel with no colour in
248	            // it. Nothing to say beyond "that did not work".
249	            NSSound.beep()
250	            return
251	        }
252	        let binding = inspector.binding
253	        guard binding.videoClips.map({ $0.id }) == session.clips else {
254	            // The selection moved while the frame was composing. Dropped
255	            // rather than applied to a clip the user never aimed at.
256	            NSSound.beep()
257	            return
258	        }
259	        binding.applyGrouped(
260	            "Chroma Key",
261	            binding.ops(video: VideoPatch(chroma: .some(session.chroma(picked: color)))))
262	    }
263	}

265	extension CanvasEyedropperSession {
266	    /// The chroma key the eyedropper stores for a pick at `point`: the
267	    /// frame's colour there, read at its code values (`FrameWriter.pickable`)
268	    /// — and in an HLG project read through the keyed clips' `reading`, so the
269	    /// stored key is the SDR colour an SDR project shows and keys through the
270	    /// shader's same reading in both outputs: the un-lift to the Rec. 709
271	    /// colour it is (spec §11 HD-13 (h)) by default, GR-15's HDR→SDR arm for
272	    /// an HLG or PQ source (HD-19 (c)).
273	    static func keyColor(
274	        at point: CGPoint, in frame: CGImage, canvas: CanvasSnapshot,
275	        reading: KeyReading = .unlift
276	    ) -> RGBA? {
277	        let picked = color(at: point, in: FrameWriter.pickable(frame), canvas: canvas)
278	        guard canvas.output == .hlg else { return picked }
279	        return picked.map(reading.pick)
280	    }

285	/// What every modal canvas mode's view shares: a transparent sheet over the
286	/// whole picture that holds first responder so Esc reaches it, wears the
287	/// crosshair, and says how to get back out in a pill. `CanvasPickOverlay`
288	/// (a click) and `CanvasRegionView` (a drag) subclass it for the gesture and
289	/// the state each mode carries; `dismissCanvasMode` tears any of them down.
290	class CanvasModeOverlay: NSView, CanvasModalMode {
291	    var onCancel: (() -> Void)?
292	
293	    static let hintTop: CGFloat = 10
294	    private static let hintPadding: CGFloat = 9
295	
296	    override init(frame frameRect: NSRect) {
297	        super.init(frame: frameRect)
298	        wantsLayer = true
299	    }
300	
301	    @available(*, unavailable)
302	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
303	        fatalError("CanvasModeOverlay does not support NSCoder")
304	    }
305	
306	    /// The canvas's own y-down space, so the hint — and a region's band — is
307	    /// placed from the top edge the way it reads.
308	    override var isFlipped: Bool { true }
309	
310	    /// Esc has to reach `keyDown`, which means holding first responder for as
311	    /// long as the mode lasts.
312	    override var acceptsFirstResponder: Bool { true }
313	
314	    /// Esc cancels. The cancel tears this view down from inside this very
315	    /// call, so the last reference to it must not be the superview's.
316	    override func keyDown(with event: NSEvent) {
317	        guard event.keyCode == 53 else {  // Esc
318	            super.keyDown(with: event)
319	            return
320	        }
321	        withExtendedLifetime(self) { onCancel?() }
322	    }
323	
324	    /// AppKit publishes no eyedropper or "draw a region" cursor, so a mode
325	    /// gets the crosshair — the same bargain `CanvasHandle.cursor` makes for
326	    /// the diagonal resize it also cannot spell.
327	    override func resetCursorRects() {
328	        addCursorRect(bounds, cursor: .crosshair)
329	    }
330	
331	    /// The view is installed before Auto Layout has given it a size, so its
332	    /// first cursor rect would be cut over an empty rectangle and the
333	    /// crosshair would never appear. Re-cut it once the size is real.
334	    override func layout() {
335	        super.layout()
336	        window?.invalidateCursorRects(for: self)
337	    }
338	
339	    /// One hint pill centred at `top`, skipped when it would not fit; answers
340	    /// its height either way, so a second pill's place does not depend on the
341	    /// first. A modal cursor is not enough on its own: the pill is what tells
342	    /// someone who armed a mode by accident that they are in one and how to
343	    /// leave it, and every mode announces itself with this one.
344	    final func drawPill(_ text: String, top: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
345	        let label = NSAttributedString(
346	            string: text,
347	            attributes: [.font: DS.sans(11), .foregroundColor: DS.textStrong])
348	        let size = label.size()
349	        let pill = CGRect(
350	            x: ((bounds.width - size.width) / 2 - Self.hintPadding).rounded(),
351	            y: top,
352	            width: (size.width + Self.hintPadding * 2).rounded(),
353	            height: (size.height + 6).rounded())
354	        guard pill.width < bounds.width else { return pill.height }
355	        let path = NSBezierPath(rect: pill)
356	        DS.chromeBackground.withAlphaComponent(0.92).setFill()
357	        path.fill()
358	        DS.accent.setStroke()
359	        path.stroke()
360	        label.draw(at: NSPoint(x: pill.minX + Self.hintPadding, y: pill.minY + 3))
361	        return pill.height
362	    }
363	
364	    /// Clears every callback before the view goes (`dismissCanvasMode`). A
365	    /// subclass clears its own, then calls this.
366	    func detachCallbacks() {
367	        onCancel = nil
368	    }
369	}

3	/// The canvas REGION mode (spec §4.2): drag a rectangle over the picture and
4	/// something is done with it. Two things, so far — `Z` adds a zoom action
5	/// that brings the rectangle to the canvas (`add_zoom_action`, road map 2's
6	/// phase 3b), and the Obscure section's "Place on Canvas" appends the
7	/// rectangle to `video.obscure` (phase 3c).
8	///
9	/// **Why one mode and not two.** Both are the same rectangle in the same
10	/// frame — spec §5.3's Q, source pixels from the centre of the layer's
11	/// cropped rect — dragged with the same gesture over the same picture. A
12	/// second overlay with a second copy of the conversion is exactly the drift
13	/// `CanvasSessions.swift` exists to prevent, so `ZoomRegionSession` carries a
14	/// `CanvasRegionPurpose` and this file branches on it in one place: the
15	/// commit at the bottom.
16	///
17	/// **Why it is not a `PreviewCanvasView` gesture**, and why every piece below
18	/// has the shape it has: `EditorViewController+Eyedropper.swift` argues it in
19	/// full and this file follows it deliberately rather than inventing a second
20	/// shape for a modal canvas mode. The overlay's PRESENCE is the mode (an
21	/// extension can hold no state, and a mode outlives a drag, so it is not a
22	/// canvas session); it is installed through `armCanvasMode`, the one place
23	/// that keeps two modal overlays from stacking; it takes first responder so
24	/// Esc reaches it; it clears its callbacks before it is torn down from inside
25	/// its own event handler; it hands focus back to the canvas overlay on the way
26	/// out; and a `sync…` hook closes it when the selection it was armed for
27	/// moves.
28	///
29	/// **The one thing it does differently.** The eyedropper takes a click and
30	/// this takes a DRAG, so the session lives on the view between mouse-down and
31	/// mouse-up, and the view is given five one-line closures instead of two: two
32	/// coordinate conversions (only `PreviewCanvasView` may map points to canvas
33	/// pixels, spec §11), the resolved frame it draws while dragging, and the two
34	/// outcomes. None of them holds logic; each forwards to a named method here.
35	extension EditorViewController {
36	    /// The armed region mode. Nil is the answer to "is the mode on".
37	    var canvasRegion: CanvasRegionView? {
38	        canvasContainer.subviews.compactMap { $0 as? CanvasRegionView }.first
39	    }
40	
41	    // MARK: - Commands
42	
43	    /// `Z`, and the action lane's Zoom to Region button.
44	    ///
45	    /// It TOGGLES, which the eyedropper had to learn the hard way: once focus
46	    /// has left the overlay — a click in the inspector, a menu — Esc no
47	    /// longer reaches it and the key that armed the mode is the only way back
48	    /// out. Pressing it again while the OTHER purpose is armed switches
49	    /// purpose rather than leaving two half-armed modes to reason about.
50	    @objc func zoomToRegion(_ sender: Any?) { toggleRegionMode(.zoom) }
51	
52	    /// The Obscure section's "Place on Canvas": the same band, appended to
53	    /// `video.obscure` instead of turned into an action.
54	    @objc func placeObscureRegion(_ sender: Any?) { toggleRegionMode(.obscure) }
55	
56	    /// The Actions section's "Zoom Back": the null-region form of the same
57	    /// op, at the playhead. No rectangle to drag, so no mode.
58	    @objc func zoomBack(_ sender: Any?) { zoomBackCommand() }
59	
60	    private func toggleRegionMode(_ purpose: CanvasRegionPurpose) {
61	        if let armed = canvasRegion {
62	            let again = armed.purpose == purpose
63	            endRegionMode()
64	            if again { return }
65	        }
66	        beginRegionMode(purpose)
67	    }
68	
69	    /// Arms the mode over the canvas pane.
70	    ///
71	    /// It refuses rather than putting up a crosshair that could only ever
72	    /// beep — `beginChromaEyedropper`'s rule, and `addActionAtPlayheadCommand`
73	    /// already refuses an action when the playhead is off the clip. There has
74	    /// to be exactly one clip selected (a region belongs to one layer's
75	    /// source pixels; two clips would be two different rectangles), it has to
76	    /// be drawing at the playhead (`regionTarget` asks the canvas, so a
77	    /// clip hidden behind an in/out range or on a locked track says no), and
78	    /// an obscure region needs a free slot.
79	    private func beginRegionMode(_ purpose: CanvasRegionPurpose) {
80	        guard let target = regionTarget(), previewCanvas != nil else {
81	            NSSound.beep()
82	            return
83	        }
84	        if purpose == .obscure, obscureRegions().count >= ObscureProps.max {
85	            NSSound.beep()
86	            return
87	        }
88	        let region = CanvasRegionView(
89	            purpose: purpose, clip: target.id, note: regionNote(purpose, clip: target.id))
90	        // One-line forwards only (app/CLAUDE.md).
91	        region.canvasPoint = { [weak self] point in self?.canvasPixel(atWindow: point) }
92	        region.viewPoint = { [weak self] point in self?.regionViewPoint(point) ?? point }
93	        region.resolvedFrame = { [weak self] session in self?.regionResolvedFrame(session) }
94	        region.onCommit = { [weak self] session in self?.regionCommitted(session) }
95	        region.onCancel = { [weak self] in self?.endRegionMode() }
96	        // The one door in (`EditorViewController+Eyedropper.swift`): it ends an
97	        // armed eyedropper on the way, so the two modes cannot stack.
98	        armCanvasMode(region)
99	    }
100	
101	    /// Disarms it, from Esc, from a second press of the key or the button,
102	    /// from a completed drag, and from `syncRegionMode`.
103	    func endRegionMode() { dismissCanvasMode(canvasRegion) }
104	
105	    /// Called from `refreshCanvas`, beside `syncChromaEyedropper`: the mode is
106	    /// armed for ONE clip, so the moment the selection stops being that clip
107	    /// — or the playhead leaves it, which would put the action's start off the
108	    /// clip — it is aimed at nothing and closes itself.
109	    func syncRegionMode() {
110	        guard let region = canvasRegion else { return }
111	        guard regionTarget()?.id != region.clip else {
112	            // Still aimed at the same clip — but the NOTE is about that
113	            // clip's `during`, not about the moment the mode was armed, and
114	            // Clip ▸ Motion ▸ During, an undo and an agent's `set_video` can
115	            // all add or clear one while the band is up. So it is re-read
116	            // here, where every `refreshCanvas` passes.
117	            region.note = regionNote(region.purpose, clip: region.clip)
118	            return
119	        }
120	        endRegionMode()
121	    }
122	
123	    /// The band's second pill for one clip, or nil: a During motion moves the
124	    /// clip under a zoom solved without it (spec §11, R5-4), and only a zoom
125	    /// is solved.
126	    private func regionNote(_ purpose: CanvasRegionPurpose, clip: UInt32) -> String? {
127	        guard purpose == .zoom else { return nil }
128	        let during = document?.editedProject.snapshot.clip(clip)?.videoProps.motion?.during
129	        return during != nil ? CanvasRegionView.duringNote : nil
130	    }
131	
132	    /// `add_zoom_action` with no region, at the playhead: the clip goes back
133	    /// to its own base `scale`, `x` and `y` over the action's span. The core
134	    /// reads an absent and an explicit null region the same way; the op
135	    /// builder sends the null so a saved call says which it meant.
136	    private func zoomBackCommand() {
137	        guard let document = document, let box = regionTarget(),
138	              let clip = document.editedProject.snapshot.clip(box.id)
139	        else {
140	            NSSound.beep()
141	            return
142	        }
143	        let at = clip.clipTime(document.playhead)
144	        document.applyEdit("Zoom Back", .addZoomAction(clip: clip.id, at: at, region: nil))
145	        selectAddedAction(on: clip.id, at: at, countBefore: clip.actions.count)
146	    }
147	
148	    // MARK: - What the mode is aimed at
149	
150	    /// The one layer a region may be drawn on: the single selected clip, on
151	    /// screen at the playhead and not on a locked track.
152	    ///
153	    /// It is answered as a `CanvasLayerBox` rather than a `ClipSnapshot`
154	    /// because the box IS the question — it exists only for a clip the recipe
155	    /// put on the canvas at this instant, and it carries the EVALUATED
156	    /// transform the rectangle has to be measured through
157	    /// (`CanvasLayerBox.sourcePoint` says why that is the opposite of every
158	    /// other canvas session).
159	    private func regionTarget() -> CanvasLayerBox? {
160	        guard let document = document, document.selection.count == 1,
161	              let id = document.selection.first,
162	              let clip = document.editedProject.snapshot.clip(id), clip.contains(document.playhead),
163	              let box = previewCanvas?.box(for: id), !box.locked
164	        else { return nil }
165	        return box
166	    }
167	
168	    /// The obscure list the mode would append to — the first selected clip
169	    /// with pixels, read through the binding so a playhead inside an action
170	    /// reads that action's end state and not the base props.
171	    private func obscureRegions() -> [ObscureProps] {
172	        inspector?.binding.videoProps.obscure ?? []
173	    }
174	
175	    // MARK: - The overlay's five questions
176	
177	    /// The inverse, landed in the OVERLAY's own coordinates — which are the
178	    /// canvas view's today (the overlay fills the canvas, both are flipped),
179	    /// but the conversion is spelled out rather than assumed.
180	    private func regionViewPoint(_ point: CGPoint) -> CGPoint {
181	        guard let canvas = previewCanvas, let region = canvasRegion else { return point }
182	        return region.convert(canvas.canvasToView(point), from: canvas)
183	    }
184	
185	    /// The rectangle the canvas will actually be showing once this zoom lands,
186	    /// in canvas pixels — what the overlay strokes beside the band so a
187	    /// freely dragged rectangle does not have to be guessed at.
188	    private func regionResolvedFrame(_ session: ZoomRegionSession) -> CGRect? {
189	        guard let box = previewCanvas?.box(for: session.clip),
190	              let source = session.sourceRect(in: box)
191	        else { return nil }
192	        return session.frameRect(in: box, source: source)
193	    }
194	
195	    // MARK: - The commit
196	
197	    /// One finished drag. `mouseUp` is an AppKit event, so both branches
198	    /// commit through the ordinary (non-grouped) door and each is ONE undo
199	    /// step; the eyedropper needs `applyGrouped` only because its answer comes
200	    /// back off a queue.
201	    ///
202	    /// A band too small to mean anything leaves the mode ARMED and beeps —
203	    /// a stray click is a miss, not a decision, which is the rule the
204	    /// eyedropper states for a click that landed off the picture.
205	    private func regionCommitted(_ session: ZoomRegionSession) {
206	        guard let box = previewCanvas?.box(for: session.clip),
207	              let region = session.region(in: box)
208	        else {
209	            NSSound.beep()
210	            return
211	        }
212	        switch session.purpose {
213	        case .zoom:
214	            commitZoom(session, region: region)
215	        case .obscure:
216	            commitObscure(session, region: region)
217	        }
218	    }
219	
220	    /// `add_zoom_action` at the playhead in CLIP time. `fit` unless ⇧ was
221	    /// held, and no `curve`, so the core's `ease_in_out` applies rather than
222	    /// `Curve.default`'s `linear`.
223	    private func commitZoom(_ session: ZoomRegionSession, region: ZoomRegion) {
224	        guard let document = document, let clip = document.editedProject.snapshot.clip(session.clip),
225	              clip.contains(document.playhead)
226	        else {
227	            NSSound.beep()
228	            return
229	        }
230	        endRegionMode()
231	        let at = clip.clipTime(document.playhead)
232	        document.applyEdit(
233	            "Zoom to Region",
234	            .addZoomAction(
235	                clip: clip.id, at: at, region: region, fit: session.fill ? .fill : .fit))
236	        selectAddedAction(on: clip.id, at: at, countBefore: clip.actions.count)
237	    }
238	
239	    /// One more `video.obscure` entry, with the rest of its fields at the
240	    /// defaults the Add button uses.
241	    ///
242	    /// It goes through the INSPECTOR BINDING and not straight to the
243	    /// document, because the binding is the one place that knows an edit made
244	    /// while the playhead sits inside an action belongs to that action's end
245	    /// state (§4.3) — and an animated obscure region is precisely what phase
246	    /// 3c's list-interpolation rule exists for, so bypassing it would break
247	    /// the feature silently.
248	    private func commitObscure(_ session: ZoomRegionSession, region: ZoomRegion) {
249	        guard let inspector = inspector, inspector.binding.ids == [session.clip] else {
250	            // The selection moved out from under the drag.
251	            NSSound.beep()
252	            return
253	        }
254	        let binding = inspector.binding
255	        var next = binding.videoProps.obscure
256	        guard next.count < ObscureProps.max else {
257	            NSSound.beep()
258	            return
259	        }
260	        next.append(
261	            ObscureProps(
262	                x: region.x, y: region.y, width: region.width, height: region.height))
263	        endRegionMode()
264	        binding.apply("Obscure Region", binding.ops(video: VideoPatch(obscure: next)))
265	    }

276	/// `CanvasOverlayView` keeps with `PreviewCanvasView`, and the reason the
277	/// five closures below take and answer plain points and rectangles.
278	final class CanvasRegionView: CanvasModeOverlay {
279	    /// What the band is for. Read here only for the hint pill; the commit
280	    /// branches on the session's copy.
281	    let purpose: CanvasRegionPurpose
282	    /// The clip the mode was armed for.
283	    let clip: UInt32
284	    /// A second hint pill under the first; nil draws none. A `var` because
285	    /// what it says is a fact about the CLIP, which can change while the mode
286	    /// is armed — `syncRegionMode` re-reads it on every `refreshCanvas`.
287	    var note: String? {
288	        didSet {
289	            if note != oldValue { needsDisplay = true }
290	        }
291	    }
292	    /// Live between mouse-down and mouse-up, and nil either side of it.
293	    private(set) var session: ZoomRegionSession?
294	
295	    /// A WINDOW point as canvas pixels; nil when there is no canvas to ask.
296	    var canvasPoint: ((CGPoint) -> CGPoint?)?
297	    /// A canvas point in this view's own coordinates.
298	    var viewPoint: ((CGPoint) -> CGPoint)?
299	    /// The rectangle the zoom will frame, in canvas pixels.
300	    var resolvedFrame: ((ZoomRegionSession) -> CGRect?)?
301	    var onCommit: ((ZoomRegionSession) -> Void)?
302	
303	    private static let zoomHint = "Drag a rectangle to zoom to it · ⇧ fills · Esc to cancel"
304	    private static let obscureHint = "Drag a rectangle to obscure · Esc to cancel"
305	    static let duringNote = "This clip has During motion — the zoom is solved without it"
306	    /// The band's own stroke, and the resolved frame's at a lower alpha —
307	    /// the same ink, because they are two readings of one rectangle.
308	    private static let frameAlpha: CGFloat = 0.45
309	
310	    init(purpose: CanvasRegionPurpose, clip: UInt32, note: String? = nil) {
311	        self.purpose = purpose
312	        self.clip = clip
313	        self.note = note
314	        super.init(frame: .zero)
315	    }
316	
317	    @available(*, unavailable)
318	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
319	        fatalError("CanvasRegionView does not support NSCoder")
320	    }

323	
324	    /// The press starts the band wherever it landed — including in the void
325	    /// around the picture. A region's centre is allowed outside the layer
326	    /// (the core asks only that x and y be finite), and dragging in from the
327	    /// margin to catch the edge of the frame is the ordinary way to do it.
328	    override func mouseDown(with event: NSEvent) {
329	        guard let point = canvasPoint?(event.locationInWindow) else {
330	            NSSound.beep()
331	            return
332	        }
333	        session = ZoomRegionSession(
334	            purpose: purpose, clip: clip, anchor: point, current: point,
335	            fill: event.modifierFlags.contains(.shift))
336	        needsDisplay = true

347	        track(event)
348	        guard let finished = session else { return }
349	        session = nil

351	    }

353	    /// ⇧ is read at every step rather than latched at the press, so the
354	    /// choice between fit and fill can be made while the band is being drawn
355	    /// and the resolved frame answers it as it is made.
356	    private func track(_ event: NSEvent) {
357	        guard var live = session, let point = canvasPoint?(event.locationInWindow) else { return }
358	        live.update(point: point, fill: event.modifierFlags.contains(.shift))
359	        session = live

361	    }

363	    /// Esc drops a band in progress BEFORE the base runs `onCancel`, so the
364	    /// mode never ends with a live session on it.
365	    override func keyDown(with event: NSEvent) {
366	        if event.keyCode == 53 { session = nil }
367	        super.keyDown(with: event)
368	    }

370	    override func detachCallbacks() {
371	        canvasPoint = nil
372	        viewPoint = nil
373	        resolvedFrame = nil

378	    // MARK: Drawing
379	
380	    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
381	        drawBand()
382	        drawHint()
383	    }
384	
385	    /// The band, and — for a zoom — the rectangle it resolves to.
386	    ///
387	    /// Both are AXIS-ALIGNED in canvas space (the band by construction, the
388	    /// frame because a zoom changes a layer's scale and position and never
389	    /// its angle), and the canvas-to-view mapping is a scale and a
390	    /// translation, so two converted corners describe each of them. Nothing
391	    /// here is rotated, which is why the marquee's flat rectangle is honest
392	    /// even over a turned clip.
393	    private func drawBand() {
394	        guard let session = session, let convert = viewPoint else { return }
395	        let band = rect(from: convert(session.anchor), to: convert(session.current))
396	        guard band.width >= 1, band.height >= 1 else { return }
397	        let path = NSBezierPath(rect: band.insetBy(dx: 0.5, dy: 0.5))
398	        DS.selectionFill.setFill()
399	        path.fill()
400	        DS.marquee.setStroke()
401	        path.stroke()
402	
403	        guard let canvasFrame = resolvedFrame?(session) else { return }
404	        let frame = rect(
405	            from: convert(CGPoint(x: canvasFrame.minX, y: canvasFrame.minY)),
406	            to: convert(CGPoint(x: canvasFrame.maxX, y: canvasFrame.maxY)))
407	        guard frame.width >= 1, frame.height >= 1 else { return }
408	        let ghost = NSBezierPath(rect: frame.insetBy(dx: 0.5, dy: 0.5))
409	        // Dashed as well as dimmed: the two rectangles coincide on one axis
410	        // under `fit`, and a solid stroke at a lower alpha under a solid one
411	        // reads as a rendering artefact rather than as a second rectangle.
412	        let dash: [CGFloat] = [4, 3]
413	        ghost.setLineDash(dash, count: dash.count, phase: 0)
414	        DS.marquee.withAlphaComponent(Self.frameAlpha).setStroke()
415	        ghost.stroke()
416	    }
417	
418	    private func rect(from a: CGPoint, to b: CGPoint) -> CGRect {
419	        CGRect(
420	            x: min(a.x, b.x), y: min(a.y, b.y), width: abs(b.x - a.x), height: abs(b.y - a.y))
421	    }
422	
423	    /// The mode's hint, and the During note under it: two of the base's
424	    /// pills (`drawPill`), so every canvas mode announces itself the same way.
425	    private func drawHint() {
426	        let hint = purpose == .zoom ? Self.zoomHint : Self.obscureHint
427	        let height = drawPill(hint, top: Self.hintTop)
428	        // 6 pt between the two pills: a gap that reads as two lines of one hint.
429	        if let note = note { _ = drawPill(note, top: Self.hintTop + height + 6) }
430	    }
431	}

70	        else { return }

3	/// What a canvas gesture edits (spec §11 CI-13): the clip's BASE props, or
4	/// the selected action's END state — the same choice the inspector's fields
5	/// make (CI-2), so a drag, a nudge and a typed value all write one place.
6	///
7	/// It reaches the canvas as a value on two channels: the refresh that already
8	/// follows a selection (`EditorViewController.refreshCanvas`) and the
9	/// playhead's own path (`canvasPlayheadMoved`, since the entry rule selects
10	/// an action without a refresh). A gesture captures it at mouse-down as
11	/// `PreviewCanvasView.gestureTarget` and writes through that for every tick,
12	/// and the sessions in `CanvasSessions.swift` ask it for their ops rather
13	/// than naming `set_video` themselves. A multi-selection is always `.base`:
14	/// no action is selected then (CI-1).
15	///
16	/// **The box on screen is still the frame at the PLAYHEAD.** A gesture
17	/// STARTS from `start(of:in:)` — the end state, for the selected action's
18	/// clip — and moves it by the pointer's travel: the inspector's "fields show
19	/// the value they write", carried to the handles.
20	struct CanvasEditTarget: Equatable {
21	    struct Selected: Equatable {
22	        let clip: UInt32
23	        let action: UInt32
24	        /// The action's end in CLIP time (`ActionSnapshot.endTime`).
25	        let endTime: Ticks
26	    }
27	
28	    /// What a gesture starts from: the end state for `selected.clip`, the
29	    /// base for any other clip. `text` is carried because a text clip's
30	    /// wrap-width drag reads it (`PreviewCanvasView.beginScale`).
31	    struct Start {
32	        let video: VideoProps
33	        let text: TextProps?
34	    }
35	
36	    /// nil: base props.
37	    let selected: Selected?
38	
39	    static let base = CanvasEditTarget(selected: nil)
40	
41	    /// The document's mode: the selected action of `singleSelectedClip`,
42	    /// else `.base`.
43	    static func current(_ document: ProjectDocument) -> CanvasEditTarget {
44	        guard let clip = document.singleSelectedClip,
45	              let action = document.selectedActionSnapshot
46	        else { return .base }
47	        return CanvasEditTarget(
48	            selected: Selected(clip: clip.id, action: action.id, endTime: action.endTime))
49	    }
50	
51	    /// The action this target writes on `clip`, nil when `clip` is written
52	    /// at its base.
53	    private func action(on clip: UInt32) -> UInt32? {
54	        guard let selected, selected.clip == clip else { return nil }
55	        return selected.action
56	    }
57	
58	    /// `set_action_end` for the selected action's clip, `set_video` for any
59	    /// other. The typed builder lifts a `.some(nil)` into `off` (CI-14).
60	    func op(video patch: VideoPatch, clip: UInt32) -> ReelOp {
61	        guard let action = action(on: clip) else { return .setVideo(clips: [clip], patch: patch) }
62	        return .setActionEnd(clip: clip, action: action, patch: ActionPatch(video: patch))
63	    }
64	
65	    /// The same rule for a text clip's wrap width.
66	    func op(text patch: TextPatch, clip: UInt32) -> ReelOp {
67	        guard let action = action(on: clip) else { return .setText(clips: [clip], patch: patch) }
68	        return .setActionEnd(clip: clip, action: action, patch: ActionPatch(text: patch))
69	    }
70	
71	    /// `clip_state` at `clip.start + endTime` decoded through
72	    /// `InspectorBinding.decode` — the inspector's own read of an END state,
73	    /// video and text from ONE call — for `selected.clip`; the clip's base
74	    /// props otherwise. A group the core does not answer falls back to base.
75	    func start(of clip: ClipSnapshot, in project: ReelProject?) -> Start {
76	        guard let selected, selected.clip == clip.id,
77	              let raw = project?.clipState(clip.id, at: clip.start + selected.endTime)
78	        else { return Start(video: clip.videoProps, text: clip.text) }
79	        return Start(
80	            video: InspectorBinding.decode(VideoProps.self, raw["video"]) ?? clip.videoProps,
81	            text: InspectorBinding.decode(TextProps.self, raw["text"]) ?? clip.text)
82	    }
83	
84	    /// The target a SCALE on `clip` starts from and writes: `.base` for a
85	    /// shape, whose scale is its box — `set_shape` has no action form, and
86	    /// the `set_video` that pins the pivot must land beside it on the same
87	    /// state (CI-13) — and `self` for anything else.
88	    func forScale(of clip: ClipSnapshot) -> CanvasEditTarget {
89	        if case .shape = clip.source { return .base }
90	        return self
91	    }
92	}

96	    /// rectangle the crop is taken out of (`CanvasLayerBox.uncroppedRect`,
97	    /// a session's start rect).
98	    var uncropped: VideoProps {
99	        var next = self
100	        next.crop = .zero
101	        return next
102	    }
103	}

7	/// adjustment clip — rendered with the `behind` option, so the clip's own
8	/// grade and every canvas layer in front of it are left out — and the
9	/// ranges are centred on that pixel (`ColorQualifier.picked`). One undo
10	/// step, "Qualifier"; Esc, a second press of the button, or a selection
11	/// change cancels.
12	///
13	/// The pixel is re-rendered rather than read off the screen, and off the
14	/// main thread, for the eyedropper's reasons (`+Eyedropper`): the commit
15	/// that follows is OFF-EVENT, so it goes through `applyGrouped`.

18	    private static let qualifierPickQueue = DispatchQueue(
19	        label: "com.kgalligan.framejob.qualifier-pick", qos: .userInitiated)

33	            endQualifierPick()
34	            return

37	            NSSound.beep()

60	        let current = inspector?.binding.clips.map { $0.id } ?? []
61	        guard current != picker.clips else { return }

69	        guard let document = document, previewCanvas != nil, let picker = qualifierPick
70	        else { return }
71	        guard let target = pickedCanvasPixel(atWindow: point) else {
72	            // A click in the void is a miss, not a decision: the mode stays.

3	/// What a canvas gesture edits (spec §11 CI-13): the clip's BASE props, or
4	/// the selected action's END state — the same choice the inspector's fields
5	/// make (CI-2), so a drag, a nudge and a typed value all write one place.
6	///
7	/// It reaches the canvas as a value on two channels: the refresh that already
8	/// follows a selection (`EditorViewController.refreshCanvas`) and the
9	/// playhead's own path (`canvasPlayheadMoved`, since the entry rule selects
10	/// an action without a refresh). A gesture captures it at mouse-down as
11	/// `PreviewCanvasView.gestureTarget` and writes through that for every tick,
12	/// and the sessions in `CanvasSessions.swift` ask it for their ops rather
13	/// than naming `set_video` themselves. A multi-selection is always `.base`:
14	/// no action is selected then (CI-1).
15	///
16	/// **The box on screen is still the frame at the PLAYHEAD.** A gesture
17	/// STARTS from `start(of:in:)` — the end state, for the selected action's
18	/// clip — and moves it by the pointer's travel: the inspector's "fields show
19	/// the value they write", carried to the handles.
20	struct CanvasEditTarget: Equatable {
21	    struct Selected: Equatable {
22	        let clip: UInt32
23	        let action: UInt32
24	        /// The action's end in CLIP time (`ActionSnapshot.endTime`).
25	        let endTime: Ticks
26	    }
27	
28	    /// What a gesture starts from: the end state for `selected.clip`, the
29	    /// base for any other clip. `text` is carried because a text clip's
30	    /// wrap-width drag reads it (`PreviewCanvasView.beginScale`).
31	    struct Start {
32	        let video: VideoProps
33	        let text: TextProps?
34	    }
35	
36	    /// nil: base props.
37	    let selected: Selected?
38	
39	    static let base = CanvasEditTarget(selected: nil)
40	
41	    /// The document's mode: the selected action of `singleSelectedClip`,
42	    /// else `.base`.
43	    static func current(_ document: ProjectDocument) -> CanvasEditTarget {
44	        guard let clip = document.singleSelectedClip,
45	              let action = document.selectedActionSnapshot
46	        else { return .base }
47	        return CanvasEditTarget(
48	            selected: Selected(clip: clip.id, action: action.id, endTime: action.endTime))
49	    }
50	
51	    /// The action this target writes on `clip`, nil when `clip` is written
52	    /// at its base.
53	    private func action(on clip: UInt32) -> UInt32? {
54	        guard let selected, selected.clip == clip else { return nil }
55	        return selected.action
56	    }
57	
58	    /// `set_action_end` for the selected action's clip, `set_video` for any
59	    /// other. The typed builder lifts a `.some(nil)` into `off` (CI-14).
60	    func op(video patch: VideoPatch, clip: UInt32) -> ReelOp {
61	        guard let action = action(on: clip) else { return .setVideo(clips: [clip], patch: patch) }
62	        return .setActionEnd(clip: clip, action: action, patch: ActionPatch(video: patch))
63	    }
64	
65	    /// The same rule for a text clip's wrap width.
66	    func op(text patch: TextPatch, clip: UInt32) -> ReelOp {
67	        guard let action = action(on: clip) else { return .setText(clips: [clip], patch: patch) }
68	        return .setActionEnd(clip: clip, action: action, patch: ActionPatch(text: patch))
69	    }
70	
71	    /// `clip_state` at `clip.start + endTime` decoded through
72	    /// `InspectorBinding.decode` — the inspector's own read of an END state,
73	    /// video and text from ONE call — for `selected.clip`; the clip's base
74	    /// props otherwise. A group the core does not answer falls back to base.
75	    func start(of clip: ClipSnapshot, in project: ReelProject?) -> Start {
76	        guard let selected, selected.clip == clip.id,
77	              let raw = project?.clipState(clip.id, at: clip.start + selected.endTime)
78	        else { return Start(video: clip.videoProps, text: clip.text) }
79	        return Start(
80	            video: InspectorBinding.decode(VideoProps.self, raw["video"]) ?? clip.videoProps,
81	            text: InspectorBinding.decode(TextProps.self, raw["text"]) ?? clip.text)
82	    }
83	
84	    /// The target a SCALE on `clip` starts from and writes: `.base` for a
85	    /// shape, whose scale is its box — `set_shape` has no action form, and
86	    /// the `set_video` that pins the pivot must land beside it on the same
87	    /// state (CI-13) — and `self` for anything else.
88	    func forScale(of clip: ClipSnapshot) -> CanvasEditTarget {
89	        if case .shape = clip.source { return .base }
90	        return self
91	    }
92	}

97	    /// a session's start rect).

99	        var next = self
100	        next.crop = .zero
101	        return next
102	    }

/// Every band, in time order, by fraction of the clip — inset 4 pt top
    /// and bottom, at least 2 pt wide.
    func bandRects() -> [(id: UInt32, rect: CGRect)] {
        guard let clip = clip, clip.duration > 0 else { return [] }
        let lane = laneRect
        let span = CGFloat(clip.duration)
        return ActionBands.ordered(clip).map { action in
            let from = lane.minX + lane.width * CGFloat(action.start) / span
            let to = lane.minX + lane.width * CGFloat(action.endTime) / span
            return (
                action.id,
                CGRect(x: from, y: lane.minY + 4, width: max(to - from, 2), height: lane.height - 8)
            )
        }
    }

    // MARK: Building

    private func buildButtons() {
        let specs: [(String, String, String, Selector)] = [
            ("plus.magnifyingglass", "+", "Zoom to Region (Z)",
             #selector(EditorViewController.zoomToRegion(_:))),
            ("minus.magnifyingglass", "−", "Zoom Back",
             #selector(EditorViewController.zoomBack(_:))),
            ("plus", "+", "Add Action (⌥⌘K)",
             #selector(EditorViewController.addActionAtPlayhead(_:))),
        ]
        var trailing = trailingAnchor
        var constant = -Self.side
        for (index, spec) in specs.enumerated().reversed() {
            let button = GhostButton(
                symbol: spec.0, fallback: spec.1, caption: nil, tooltip: spec.2,
                action: #selector(buttonPressed(_:)), size: NSSize(width: 20, height: 18),
                pointSize: 13)
            button.target = self
            button.tag = index
            button.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
            addSubview(button)
            NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
                button.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: topAnchor, constant: Self.top),
                button.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: trailing, constant: constant),
            ])
            trailing = button.leadingAnchor
            constant = -2
        }
        commands = specs.map { $0.3 }
    }

title: Nests
description: Collapse several clips into one clip that moves, trims, fades and transforms as a group, and open it back out when you're done.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A nest collapses several clips into one clip that stands for the group. From then on the group moves, trims, fades and transforms as one thing, and the clips inside stay as you built them.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Nest', 'Clip ▸ Un-nest']}
  keys={['⌘G', '⇧⌘G']}
  tools={['nest', 'unnest']}
/>

## Make a nest

<Steps>

1. Select the clips.

2. Press <kbd>⌘G</kbd>, or choose **Clip ▸ Nest**.

</Steps>

The clips are replaced by one nest clip, which is selected so you can move or transform it straight away. The nest is one undo step, called Nest.

The nest clip goes on the front-most track the selection used, and runs from the earliest start to the latest end, including any gaps. A matte track is the exception: the nest clip goes on the front-most track that isn't a matte. See [Mattes inside nests](/canvas/mattes-in-nests/).

fixed.now: The clip must also have a box on the canvas, and Place on Canvas also beeps when the clip already has four regions.

fixed.was: A mode ends when you finish the drag, with no exception.
fixed.now: Added that a rectangle less than 6 canvas pixels wide or high beeps and the mode stays armed.

fixed.was: Only an adjustment clip was said never to have a selection frame.
fixed.now: A nest clip has none either, and a click on its picture goes through to whatever is behind. Links to Layers.

fixed.was: The matte clip is 'the front-most clip inside that box'.
fixed.now: 'Because it's in front of the clip it cuts', which stays true when another track sits in front of the matte track.

fixed.was: The scale table's first row included nest clips.
fixed.now: Nest removed from the row. New Good to know bullet: a nest clip has no box on the canvas, so place it on the Picture tab.

fixed.was: 'The opposite handle stays pinned in place', with no exception.
fixed.now: Added that on a cropped clip the pinned point is on the uncropped picture, so the cropped edge opposite can shift.

fixed.was: Esc doesn't cancel while ⌥ or ⌘ is held.
fixed.now: While ⌥, ⌃ or ⌘ is held, because every modifier but ⇧ blocks it.

fixed.was: Snap targets were 'every other layer drawn at the playhead'.
fixed.now: 'Every other clip with a box on the canvas at the playhead', plus a line saying a nest clip has no box, so it isn't a target.

guide_errors: docs/guide/canvas-and-layers.md:60-61 lists '← → ↑ ↓ (canvas focused)' as a 1-pixel nudge and '⇧ + arrow' as 10 pixels. Arrow keys never nudge. Arrow-key events should carry the numeric-pad and function flags (a standard AppKit fact, implied by the exception at app/Sources/EditorWindow.swift:123-129), so the guard at app/Sources/PreviewCanvasView.swift:663 returns false, nudge is unreachable, and the keys fall through to frame stepping at app/Sources/EditorViewController.swift:744-751.
docs/guide/canvas-and-layers.md:114 says 'an arrow-key nudge' edits the selected action's end state. No such nudge reaches the canvas, for the same reason.

docs/guide/canvas-and-layers.md:70 groups nest clips with the clips scaled by canvas handles. A nest clip has no canvas box at the timeline level, so it has no handles (app/Sources/CanvasSessions.swift:298-307).
